## JSON

Converts between JSON text and the builtin JSON type.

### JSON.decode

```
JSON.decode(string) -> result[JSON,string]
```

Parses JSON text into the JSON type, whose constructors are JSON.null, JSON.boolean, JSON.integer, JSON.float, JSON.string, JSON.list and JSON.object.

```elixir
alx> JSON.decode("[1, true]")
ok(JSON.list([JSON.integer(1), JSON.boolean(true)]))
alx> case JSON.decode("{") do
...>   ok(_) -> "valid"
...>   error(_) -> "invalid"
...> end
"invalid"
```

### JSON.decode!

```
JSON.decode!(string) -> JSON
```

Parses JSON text; fails when it is invalid.

```elixir
alx> JSON.decode!("{\"a\": null}")
JSON.object(%{"a" => JSON.null})
```

### JSON.encode

```
JSON.encode(a) -> result[string,string]
```

Writes any value as JSON: ok(text), or error(reason) for a value with no JSON form, such as an infinite float. Structs become objects by field name, maps objects with their keys as text, lists, sets and tuples arrays, atoms strings, none null and some(x) x; a variant without fields becomes its name and one with fields {"name": [fields]}. JSON.encode! takes the same values, and [pretty: true] indents the result.

```elixir
alx> JSON.encode(%{"a" => [1, 2]})
ok("{\"a\":[1,2]}")
alx> JSON.encode!({:ok, some(1.5)})
"[\"ok\",1.5]"
```

### JSON.encode!

```
JSON.encode!(a) -> string
JSON.encode!(JSON) -> string
JSON.encode!(a, list[tuple[atom,boolean]]) -> string
```

Writes a JSON value as text, with object keys in ascending order.

```elixir
alx> JSON.encode!(JSON.object(%{"name" => JSON.string("al"), "tags" => JSON.list([JSON.integer(1)])}))
"{\"name\":\"al\",\"tags\":[1]}"
```

```
Date.before?(Date, Date) -> boolean
```

```
Date.compare(Date, Date) -> atom
```

```elixir
32
```

```
Date.days_in_month(Date) -> integer
```

The number of days from the second date to the first.

```elixir
28
```

### Date.end_of_month

```
Date.end_of_month(Date) -> Date
```

The last day of the date's month.

### Date.end_of_week

### Date.from_iso8601


Parses YYYY-MM-DD text, returning ok(date) or error(reason).

### Date.from_iso8601!

```
Date.from_iso8601!(string) -> Date
```

Parses YYYY-MM-DD text; fails when it is invalid.

```elixir

~D[2026-03-18]
```

### Date.leap_year?

```
Date.leap_year?(Date) -> boolean
```

Reports whether the date falls in a leap year.

```elixir
alx> Date.leap_year?(~D[2024-01-01])
true
```

### Date.new

```
Date.new(integer, integer, integer) -> result[Date,string]
```

Builds a date from year, month and day, returning an error for a date that does not exist.

```elixir
alx> Date.new(2026, 3, 18)
ok(~D[2026-03-18])
alx> case Date.new(2026, 2, 30) do
...>   ok(_) -> "valid"
...>   error(_) -> "invalid"
...> end
"invalid"
```

### Date.new!

```
Date.new!(integer, integer, integer) -> Date
```

Builds a date from year, month and day; fails for a date that does not exist.

```elixir
alx> Date.new!(2026, 3, 18)
~D[2026-03-18]
```

### Date.quarter_of_year

```
Date.quarter_of_year(Date) -> integer
```

The quarter, from 1 to 4.

```elixir
alx> Date.quarter_of_year(~D[2026-05-01])
2
```

### Date.range

```
Date.range(Date, Date) -> stream[Date]
Date.range(Date, Date, integer) -> stream[Date]
```

The dates from one to another, inclusive, a day apart or a given number of days; backwards when the last is earlier.

```elixir
alx> Date.range(~D[2026-01-30], ~D[2026-02-01]) |> Enum.to_list()
[~D[2026-01-30], ~D[2026-01-31], ~D[2026-02-01]]
alx> Date.range(~D[2026-01-01], ~D[2026-01-31], 7) |> Enum.count()
5
```

### Date.shift

```
Date.shift(Date, Duration) -> Date
```

Moves a date by a duration of years, months, weeks and days. A month is added on the calendar: the day is kept, or becomes the last day the new month has. A duration with time units fails.

```elixir
alx> Date.shift(~D[2026-01-31], Duration.months(1))
~D[2026-02-28]
alx> Date.shift(~D[2024-02-29], Duration.add(Duration.years(1), Duration.days(1)))
~D[2025-03-01]
```

### Date.to_iso8601

```
Date.to_iso8601(Date) -> string
```

The date as YYYY-MM-DD text.

```elixir

"2026-03-18"
```

```
Date.to_string(Date) -> string
```

The date as YYYY-MM-DD text.

```elixir
alx> Date.to_string(~D[2026-03-18])

```

```

```

```
Date.week_of_year(Date) -> integer
```

The ISO 8601 week of the year, from 1 to 53.

```elixir
alx> Date.week_of_year(~D[2026-01-01])
1
```

```
NaiveDateTime.compare(NaiveDateTime, NaiveDateTime) -> atom
```

Returns :lt, :eq or :gt as the first is earlier than, equal to or later than the second.


### NaiveDateTime.from_iso8601!

```
NaiveDateTime.from_iso8601!(string) -> NaiveDateTime
```

### NaiveDateTime.new

```elixir

~N[2026-03-01 01:00:00]
```

```
NaiveDateTime.to_string(NaiveDateTime) -> string
```

```
NaiveDateTime.to_time(NaiveDateTime) -> Time
```

## DateTime

A date and time in a time zone: UTC when written ~U[2026-01-05T13:04:05Z], another zone after DateTime.shift_zone.

### DateTime.add

```
DateTime.add(DateTime, integer) -> DateTime
DateTime.add(DateTime, integer, atom) -> DateTime
```

Adds a number of seconds.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.add(~U[2026-01-05T23:59:59Z], 2)
~U[2026-01-06T00:00:01Z]
```

### DateTime.after?

```
DateTime.after?(DateTime, DateTime) -> boolean
```

Reports whether the first is later than the second.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.after?(~U[2026-01-06T00:00:00Z], ~U[2026-01-05T00:00:00Z])
true
```

### DateTime.before?

```
DateTime.before?(DateTime, DateTime) -> boolean
```

Reports whether the first is earlier than the second.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.before?(~U[2026-01-06T00:00:00Z], ~U[2026-01-05T00:00:00Z])
false
```

### DateTime.compare

```
DateTime.compare(DateTime, DateTime) -> atom
```

Returns :lt, :eq or :gt as the first is earlier than, equal to or later than the second.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.compare(~U[2026-01-06T00:00:00Z], ~U[2026-01-05T00:00:00Z])
:gt
```

### DateTime.diff

```
DateTime.diff(DateTime, DateTime) -> integer
DateTime.diff(DateTime, DateTime, atom) -> integer
```

The number of seconds from the second to the first.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.diff(~U[2026-01-05T00:01:00Z], ~U[2026-01-05T00:00:00Z])
60
```

### DateTime.from_iso8601

```
DateTime.from_iso8601(string) -> result[tuple[DateTime,integer],string]
```

Parses text with a zone offset, returning the moment in UTC with the offset in seconds.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.from_iso8601("2026-01-05T13:04:05+02:00")
ok({~U[2026-01-05T11:04:05Z], 7200})
```

### DateTime.from_naive

```
DateTime.from_naive(NaiveDateTime, string) -> result[DateTime,string]
```

Reads a date and time as the wall clock of a time zone. A time the clocks skipped moves forward by the gap, and one they repeated takes its first occurrence.

```elixir
alx> case DateTime.from_naive(~N[2026-01-05 13:00:00], "Europe/Paris") do
...>   ok(paris) -> DateTime.to_unix(paris) == DateTime.to_unix(~U[2026-01-05T12:00:00Z])
...>   error(_) -> false
...> end
true
```

### DateTime.from_naive!

```
DateTime.from_naive!(NaiveDateTime) -> DateTime
```

Interprets a naive date and time as UTC.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.from_naive!(~N[2026-01-05 13:04:05])
~U[2026-01-05T13:04:05Z]
```

### DateTime.from_unix

```
DateTime.from_unix(integer) -> result[DateTime,string]
```

The moment a number of seconds after the Unix epoch.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.from_unix(86400)
ok(~U[1970-01-02T00:00:00Z])
```

### DateTime.from_unix!

```
DateTime.from_unix!(integer) -> DateTime
```

The moment a number of seconds after the Unix epoch; fails when out of range.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.from_unix!(0)
~U[1970-01-01T00:00:00Z]
```

### DateTime.now

```
DateTime.now(string) -> result[DateTime,string]
```

The current moment in a time zone.

```elixir
alx> case DateTime.now("Asia/Tokyo") do
...>   ok(now) -> now.utc_offset
...>   error(_) -> 0
...> end
32400
```

### DateTime.shift

```
DateTime.shift(DateTime, Duration) -> DateTime
```

Moves a DateTime by a duration, staying in its time zone: calendar units move its wall clock, so a day later is the same time of day across a clock change, and time units are elapsed time.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.shift(~U[2026-01-31T12:00:00Z], Duration.months(1))
~U[2026-02-28T12:00:00Z]
alx> paris = DateTime.shift_zone!(~U[2026-03-28T11:00:00Z], "Europe/Paris")
alx> DateTime.to_iso8601(DateTime.shift(paris, Duration.days(1)))
"2026-03-29T12:00:00+02:00"
alx> DateTime.to_iso8601(DateTime.shift(paris, Duration.hours(24)))
"2026-03-29T13:00:00+02:00"
```

### DateTime.shift_zone

```
DateTime.shift_zone(DateTime, string) -> result[DateTime,string]
```

The same moment as the wall clock of another time zone shows it, by its name in the zone database, which is built into the program. An unknown name is an error.

```elixir
alx> case DateTime.shift_zone(~U[2026-01-05T12:00:00Z], "Europe/Paris") do
...>   ok(paris) -> DateTime.to_string(paris)
...>   error(reason) -> reason
...> end
"2026-01-05 13:00:00+01:00 CET Europe/Paris"
alx> DateTime.shift_zone(~U[2026-01-05T12:00:00Z], "Mars/Olympus")
error("unknown time zone \"Mars/Olympus\"")
```

### DateTime.shift_zone!

```
DateTime.shift_zone!(DateTime, string) -> DateTime
```

The same moment in another time zone; fails on an unknown zone name. The time_zone and utc_offset fields say where it is.

```elixir
alx> new_york = DateTime.shift_zone!(~U[2026-07-04T16:00:00Z], "America/New_York")
alx> DateTime.to_iso8601(new_york)
"2026-07-04T12:00:00-04:00"
alx> new_york.utc_offset
-14400
alx> DateTime.compare(new_york, ~U[2026-07-04T16:00:00Z])
:eq
alx> Calendar.strftime(new_york, "%H:%M %Z %z")
"12:00 EDT -0400"
```

### DateTime.to_date

```
DateTime.to_date(DateTime) -> Date
```

The date part.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.to_date(~U[2026-01-05T13:04:05Z])
~D[2026-01-05]
```

### DateTime.to_iso8601

```
DateTime.to_iso8601(DateTime) -> string
```

The value as ISO 8601 text, ending in Z in UTC and in the offset, such as +01:00, in another zone.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.to_iso8601(~U[2026-01-05T13:04:05Z])
"2026-01-05T13:04:05Z"
```

### DateTime.to_naive

```
DateTime.to_naive(DateTime) -> NaiveDateTime
```

The same date and time without the zone.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.to_naive(~U[2026-01-05T13:04:05Z])
~N[2026-01-05 13:04:05]
```

### DateTime.to_string

```
DateTime.to_string(DateTime) -> string
```

The value as text, ending in Z in UTC; in another zone, with the offset, the zone's abbreviation and its name.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.to_string(~U[2026-01-05T13:04:05Z])
"2026-01-05 13:04:05Z"
```

### DateTime.to_time

```
DateTime.to_time(DateTime) -> Time
```

The time part.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.to_time(~U[2026-01-05T13:04:05Z])
~T[13:04:05]
```

### DateTime.to_unix

```
DateTime.to_unix(DateTime) -> integer
```

Seconds since the Unix epoch.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.to_unix(~U[1970-01-02T00:00:00Z])
86400
```

### DateTime.truncate

```
DateTime.truncate(DateTime, atom) -> DateTime
```

Drops precision, as Time.truncate does.

```elixir
alx> DateTime.truncate(~U[2026-01-01T10:00:00.5Z], :second)
~U[2026-01-01T10:00:00Z]
```

### DateTime.utc_now

```
DateTime.utc_now() -> DateTime
```

The current moment.


## Calendar

Formatting shared by the four date and time types.

### Calendar.strftime

```
Calendar.strftime(a, string) -> string
```

Formats a Date, Time, NaiveDateTime or DateTime. Directives: %Y %y year, %m month, %d day, %j day of year, %q quarter, %u weekday number (Monday is 1), %a %A weekday name, %b %B month name, %H %I hour, %M minute, %S second, %f fraction, %p %P AM/PM, %z %Z zone, %c %x %X preferred forms, %% a percent sign. A flag after % changes padding (- none, 0 zeros, _ spaces) and a number sets the width. A directive the value has no field for fails.

Requires: a is a Date, Time, NaiveDateTime or DateTime.

```elixir
alx> Calendar.strftime(~D[2026-03-05], "%A %-d %B %Y")
"Thursday 5 March 2026"
alx> Calendar.strftime(~U[2026-03-14T15:09:26Z], "%y-%m-%d %I:%M:%S %p")
"26-03-14 03:09:26 PM"
alx> Calendar.strftime(~T[09:04:05], "%H:%M")
"09:04"
alx> Calendar.strftime(~N[2026-03-05 09:04:05], "%j %q %u %a %b %%")
"064 1 4 Thu Mar %"
```

## Duration

An amount of time per unit, for shifting dates and times: Duration.months(1), Duration.add(...).

### Duration.add

```
Duration.add(Duration, Duration) -> Duration
```

Adds two durations unit by unit. Nothing is carried from one unit to another.

```elixir
alx> Duration.add(Duration.months(1), Duration.days(10)) |> Duration.to_iso8601()
"P1M10D"
```

### Duration.days

```
Duration.days(integer) -> Duration
```

A duration of that many days; the other units are zero.

```elixir
alx> Duration.days(3).day
3
```

```
Duration.from_iso8601(string) -> result[Duration,string]
```

Parses an ISO 8601 duration such as P1Y2M3DT4H5M6S.

```elixir
alx> Duration.from_iso8601("P2Y1M4DT3H7M1.5S")
ok(%Duration{year: 2, month: 1, week: 0, day: 4, hour: 3, minute: 7, second: 1, microsecond: 500000})
alx> case Duration.from_iso8601("soon") do
...>   ok(_) -> "valid"
...>   error(_) -> "invalid"
...> end
"invalid"
```

### Duration.hours

```
Duration.hours(integer) -> Duration
```

A duration of that many hours; the other units are zero.

```elixir
alx> Duration.hours(3).hour
3
```

```

```

```elixir
3
```

### Duration.minutes

```
Duration.minutes(integer) -> Duration
```

A duration of that many minutes; the other units are zero.

```elixir
alx> Duration.minutes(3).minute
3
```

### Duration.months

```
Duration.months(integer) -> Duration
```

A duration of that many months; the other units are zero.

```elixir
3
```

### Duration.multiply

```
Duration.multiply(Duration, integer) -> Duration
```

Multiplies every unit.

```elixir

```

### Duration.negate

```
Duration.negate(Duration) -> Duration
```

The same amounts with the opposite sign, for shifting backwards.

```elixir
alx> Date.shift(~D[2026-03-31], Duration.negate(Duration.months(1)))
```

### Duration.new!

```

```

A duration from a keyword list of year:, month:, week:, day:, hour:, minute:, second: and microsecond:.

### Duration.seconds

```

```



Subtracts the second duration from the first, unit by unit.


### Duration.weeks

```
Duration.weeks(integer) -> Duration
```

A duration of that many weeks; the other units are zero.

```
Duration.years(integer) -> Duration
```

## File

Reading, writing and managing files; File.stream! reads lazily.

### File.append

```
File.append(string, string) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Appends text to a file, creating it when missing.

```elixir
alx> File.write("doc_append.txt", "a")
ok({})
alx> File.append("doc_append.txt", "b")
ok({})
alx> File.read("doc_append.txt")
ok("ab")
```

### File.chmod

```
File.chmod(string, integer) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Sets a file's permission bits, written in octal as 0o644.

```elixir
alx> path = Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "file_doc.txt")
alx> File.write(path, "z")
ok({})
alx> File.chmod(path, 0o600)
ok({})
alx> ok(stat) = File.stat(path)
alx> stat.access in [:read_write, :read]
true
```

### File.close

```
File.close(file) -> boolean
```

Closes a file opened with File.open; false when it was already closed.

```elixir
alx> path = Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "file_doc.txt")
alx> ok(f) = File.open(path, [:write])
alx> File.close(f)
true
alx> File.close(f)
false
```

### File.cp

```
File.cp(string, string) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Copies a file.

```elixir
alx> File.write!("doc_cp.txt", "data")
alx> File.cp("doc_cp.txt", "doc_cp_copy.txt")
ok({})
alx> File.read!("doc_cp_copy.txt")
"data"
```

### File.cp_r

```
File.cp_r(string, string) -> result[list[string],string]
```

Copies a file, or a directory and everything in it, and returns the paths written.

```elixir
alx> from = Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "cp_r_doc")
alx> File.rm_rf(from)
alx> File.mkdir_p(from)
alx> File.write(Path.join(from, "a.txt"), "a")
ok({})
alx> to = from <> "_copy"
alx> File.rm_rf(to)
alx> ok(written) = File.cp_r(from, to)
alx> length(written)
2
alx> File.read(Path.join(to, "a.txt"))
ok("a")
```

```
File.cwd() -> result[string,string]
```

### File.open

```
File.open(string, list[atom]) -> result[file,string]
File.open(string, list[atom], fn[file,a]) -> result[a,string]
```

Opens a file with modes: :read (the default), :write (from empty), :append, :exclusive (only a new file), with :utf8 and :binary accepted. The file belongs to the process that opened it and closes when it ends. Given a function, the file is passed to it and closed afterwards, and the result is the function's.

```elixir
alx> path = Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "file_doc.txt")
alx> ok(f) = File.open(path, [:write])
alx> IO.puts(f, "line")
ok({})
alx> File.close(f)
true
alx> File.open(path, [:read], fn file -> IO.read(file, :line) end)
ok(some("line\n"))
alx> case File.open(Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "no/such/dir/x"), [:read]) do
...>   ok(_) -> "opened"
...>   error(reason) -> reason
...> end
"enoent"
```

```
File.read(string) -> result[string,string]
```

Reads a whole file, returning ok(contents) or error(reason).

```elixir
alx> File.read("doc_read.txt")
ok("hello")
alx> case File.read("no_such_file.txt") do
...>   ok(text) -> text
...>   error(_) -> "missing"
...> end
"missing"
```

```elixir
alx> File.rmdir("doc_rmdir")
ok({})
```

### File.stat

```
File.stat(string) -> result[File.Stat,string]
```

What is known about a file: its size in bytes, type (:regular, :directory, :symlink or :other), the access this program has (:read, :write, :read_write or :none), when it last changed in seconds since 1970, and its permission bits.

```elixir
alx> path = Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "file_doc.txt")
alx> File.write(path, "12345")
ok({})
alx> ok(stat) = File.stat(path)
alx> {stat.size, stat.type}
{5, :regular}
```

### File.stream!

```
File.stream!(string) -> stream[string]
File.stream!(string, integer) -> stream[string]
```

A lazy stream of a file's lines, each keeping its line ending; with a size, of chunks of that many bytes. The file is read as the stream is consumed and closed when it ends.

```elixir
alx> File.write!("doc_stream.txt", "one\ntwo\nthree\n")
alx> File.stream!("doc_stream.txt") |> Stream.map(&String.trim(&1)) |> Enum.take(2)
["one", "two"]
alx> File.stream!("doc_stream.txt", 4) |> Enum.take(1)
["one\n"]
```

### File.touch

```
File.touch(string) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Creates an empty file, or updates the modification time of an existing one.

```elixir
alx> File.touch("doc_touch.txt")
ok({})
alx> File.exists?("doc_touch.txt")
true
```

### File.write

```
File.write(string, string) -> result[tuple[],string]
File.write(string, string, list[atom]) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Writes text to a file, replacing its contents.

```elixir
alx> File.write("doc_write.txt", "hello")
ok({})
```

### File.write!

```
File.write!(string, string)
```

Writes text to a file; fails when it cannot be written.

```elixir
alx> File.write!("doc_write_bang.txt", "hello")
alx> File.read!("doc_write_bang.txt")
"hello"
```

```
Path.absname(string) -> string
```

The path made absolute against the working directory.

An absolute path with . and .. resolved and a leading ~ replaced by the home directory.

```
Path.extname(string) -> string
```

The extension of the last component, with its dot.


```
Path.relative_to(string, string) -> string
```

The path relative to a base, or unchanged when it is not under the base.

### Path.rootname

```
Path.rootname(string) -> string
Path.rootname(string, string) -> string
```

The path without its extension, or without the given one.

### Path.safe_relative

```
Path.safe_relative(string) -> option[string]
Path.safe_relative(string, string) -> option[string]
```

A relative path cleaned of . and .., when it stays inside the directory it is relative to; none when it would leave it or is absolute. Given a directory, an absolute path inside it is made relative to it first.

### Path.split

The components of a path.

### Path.type

```
Path.type(string) -> atom
```

Whether a path is :absolute, :relative, or on Windows :volumerelative.

### Path.wildcard

The existing paths matching a glob pattern, sorted.

## IO

Standard input, output and error.

### IO.binread

```
IO.binread(integer) -> option[string]
IO.binread(file, integer) -> option[string]
```

Reads that many bytes from standard input, or from a file opened with File.open; none at the end.

```elixir
alx> ok(f) = File.open(Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "io_binread_doc.txt"), [:write])
alx> IO.write(f, "bytes")
ok({})
alx> File.close(f)
true
alx> File.open(Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "io_binread_doc.txt"), [:read], fn file -> IO.binread(file, 3) end)
ok(some("byt"))
```

### IO.gets

```
IO.gets(string) -> option[string]
```

Writes a prompt and reads one line from standard input without its line ending; none at end of input.

### IO.inspect

```
IO.inspect(a) -> a
```

Writes any value to standard output in source form and returns it, so it can sit in a pipeline.

```elixir
alx> [1, 2] |> IO.inspect() |> length()
2
```

### IO.puts

```
IO.puts(string)
IO.puts(atom, string)
IO.puts(file, string) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Writes a string to standard output, or to the device given first, :stdio or :stderr, followed by a newline. Interpolate other values: IO.puts("total: #{n}").

```elixir

alx> IO.puts("total: #{1 + 2}")
alx> IO.puts(:stderr, "to standard error")
```

### IO.read

```
IO.read(atom) -> option[string]
IO.read(integer) -> option[string]
IO.read(atom, atom) -> option[string]
IO.read(file, atom) -> option[string]
IO.read(file, integer) -> option[string]
```

Reads standard input: :line gives the next line with its newline, :eof the rest of the input, a number that many characters; none at the end. Given a file opened with File.open first, it reads that file.

```elixir
alx> ok(f) = File.open(Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "io_read_doc.txt"), [:write])
alx> IO.write(f, "one\ntwo\n")
ok({})
alx> File.close(f)
true
alx> File.open(Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "io_read_doc.txt"), [:read], fn file -> {IO.read(file, :line), IO.read(file, 2), IO.read(file, :eof)} end)
ok({some("one\n"), some("tw"), some("o\n")})
```

### IO.read_all

```
IO.read_all() -> string
```

Reads all of standard input.

### IO.read_line

```
IO.read_line() -> option[string]
```

Reads one line from standard input without its line ending; none at end of input.

### IO.stream

```
IO.stream() -> stream[string]
```

A lazy stream of the lines of standard input, each keeping its line ending.

### IO.warn

```
IO.warn(string)
```

Writes a line to standard error.

```elixir
alx> IO.warn("careful")
```

### IO.write

```
IO.write(string)
IO.write(file, string) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Writes a string to standard output without a newline.

```elixir
alx> IO.write("no newline")
```
