## URI

Percent-encoding and query strings.

### URI.append_path

```
URI.append_path(URI, string) -> URI
```

Adds a path, which starts with /, to the URI's path.

```elixir
alx> URI.to_string(URI.append_path(URI.parse("http://a.com/api"), "/v1"))
"http://a.com/api/v1"
```

### URI.append_query

```
URI.append_query(URI, string) -> URI
```

Adds a query to the URI's query, joined with &.

```elixir
alx> URI.to_string(URI.append_query(URI.parse("http://a.com/?x=1"), "y=2"))
"http://a.com/?x=1&y=2"
```

### URI.decode

```
URI.decode(string) -> result[string,string]
```

Decodes percent-encoding, returning an error for a malformed escape.

```elixir
alx> URI.decode("a%20b")
ok("a b")
alx> case URI.decode("%zz") do
...>   ok(_) -> "valid"
...>   error(_) -> "malformed"
...> end
"malformed"
```

### URI.decode_query

```
URI.decode_query(string) -> map[string,string]
```

Decodes a query string into a map; a later pair replaces an earlier one with the same key.

```elixir
alx> URI.decode_query("q=a+b&page=2")
%{"page" => "2", "q" => "a b"}
```

### URI.decode_www_form

```
URI.decode_www_form(string) -> result[string,string]
```

Decodes a form value, where + is a space.

```elixir
alx> URI.decode_www_form("a+b%26c")
ok("a b&c")
```

### URI.encode

```
URI.encode(string) -> string
```

Percent-encodes every character that is neither reserved nor unreserved in a URI, so an address keeps its structure.

```elixir
alx> URI.encode("https://example.com/a b?q=é")
"https://example.com/a%20b?q=%C3%A9"
```

### URI.encode_query

```
URI.encode_query(map[string,string]) -> string
```

Encodes a map as a query string, keys in ascending order.

```elixir
alx> URI.encode_query(%{"q" => "a b", "page" => "2"})
"page=2&q=a+b"
```

### URI.encode_www_form

```
URI.encode_www_form(string) -> string
```

Encodes text as a form value: everything but letters, digits and -_.~ is escaped, and a space becomes +.

```elixir
alx> URI.encode_www_form("a b&c=d")
"a+b%26c%3Dd"
```

### URI.merge

```
URI.merge(URI, string) -> URI
URI.merge(string, string) -> URI
```

Resolves a reference against a base URI, as a browser resolves a link.

```elixir
alx> URI.to_string(URI.merge("http://a.com/x/y", "../z?q=1"))
"http://a.com/z?q=1"
```

### URI.new

```
URI.new(string) -> result[URI,string]
```

Like URI.parse, returning an error for text that is not a well-formed address.

```elixir
alx> case URI.new("http://example.com/%zz") do
...>   ok(_) -> "valid"
...>   error(_) -> "malformed"
...> end
"malformed"
```

### URI.parse

```
URI.parse(string) -> URI
```

Splits an address into a URI struct: scheme, userinfo, host, port, path, query and fragment. Parts the address lacks are none; http, https, ws, wss and ftp get their usual port. Text that is not an address becomes a URI with only a path.

```elixir
alx> uri = URI.parse("https://ada@example.com:8443/a/b?q=1#top")
alx> {uri.scheme, uri.userinfo, uri.host, uri.port}
{some("https"), some("ada"), some("example.com"), some(8443)}
alx> {uri.path, uri.query, uri.fragment}
{"/a/b", some("q=1"), some("top")}
alx> URI.parse("http://example.com").port
some(80)
alx> URI.parse("/only/a/path").host
none
```

### URI.to_string

```
URI.to_string(URI) -> string
```

Writes a URI struct as text, leaving out the usual port of its scheme.

```elixir
alx> URI.to_string(URI.parse("https://example.com:443/a?b=1"))
"https://example.com/a?b=1"
alx> uri = URI.parse("http://example.com/a")
alx> URI.to_string(%URI{uri | path: "/b", query: some("page=2")})
"http://example.com/b?page=2"
```

## Version

Parsing and comparing semantic versions.

### Version.compare

```
Version.compare(string, string) -> atom
Version.compare(Version, Version) -> atom
```

Returns :lt, :eq or :gt as the first version is lower than, equal to or higher than the second. A pre-release is lower than its release. Fails on an invalid version.

```elixir
alx> Version.compare("1.9.0", "1.10.0")
:lt
alx> Version.compare("2.0.0-rc.1", "2.0.0")
:lt
alx> Version.compare("1.0.0-alpha.2", "1.0.0-alpha.10")
:lt
alx> Version.compare("3.1.4", "3.1.4")
:eq
```

### Version.match?

```
Version.match?(string, string) -> boolean
Version.match?(Version, string) -> boolean
Version.match?(string, Version.Requirement) -> boolean
Version.match?(Version, Version.Requirement) -> boolean
Version.match?(string, string, list[tuple[atom,boolean]]) -> boolean
```

Reports whether a version meets a requirement: comparisons with ==, !=, >, >=, <, <= and ~>, joined by and and or. ~> 2.1 allows 2.1 and later within 2; ~> 2.1.3 allows 2.1.3 and later within 2.1. Fails on an invalid version or requirement.

```elixir
alx> Version.match?("2.3.1", "~> 2.1")
true
alx> Version.match?("3.0.0", "~> 2.1")
false
alx> Version.match?("2.1.9", "~> 2.1.3")
true
alx> Version.match?("1.5.0", ">= 1.0.0 and < 2.0.0")
true
alx> Version.match?("0.9.0", ">= 1.0.0 or == 0.9.0")
true
alx> Version.match?("2.1.0-rc.1", "~> 2.0", [allow_pre: false])
false
alx> Version.match?(Version.parse!("2.3.0"), "~> 2.1")
true
```

### Version.parse

```
Version.parse(string) -> result[Version,string]
```

Parses a semantic version into a Version struct, with its pre-release identifiers and build metadata.

```elixir
alx> ok(v) = Version.parse("2.10.3")
alx> {v.major, v.minor, v.patch}
{2, 10, 3}
alx> ok(pre) = Version.parse("1.0.0-rc.1+build5")
alx> {pre.pre, pre.build}
{["rc", "1"], some("build5")}
alx> case Version.parse("1.2") do
...>   ok(_) -> "valid"
...>   error(reason) -> reason
...> end
"invalid version \"1.2\""
```

### Version.parse!

```
Version.parse!(string) -> Version
```

Parses a semantic version into a Version struct, failing when it is not one.

```elixir
alx> Version.parse!("1.2.3").minor
2
```

### Version.parse_requirement

```
Version.parse_requirement(string) -> result[Version.Requirement,string]
```

Checks a requirement once, giving a Version.Requirement to match versions against.

```elixir
alx> ok(req) = Version.parse_requirement("~> 2.0")
alx> Version.match?("2.4.0", req)
true
alx> case Version.parse_requirement("bogus") do
...>   ok(_) -> "valid"
...>   error(_) -> "invalid"
...> end
"invalid"
```

### Version.parse_requirement!

```
Version.parse_requirement!(string) -> Version.Requirement
```

Like Version.parse_requirement, failing on an invalid requirement.

```elixir
alx> Version.match?("1.0.0", Version.parse_requirement!(">= 1.0.0"))
true
```

### Version.to_string

```
Version.to_string(Version) -> string
```

Writes a Version back as text.

```elixir
alx> Version.to_string(%Version{major: 2, minor: 0, patch: 1, pre: ["beta", "2"]})
"2.0.1-beta.2"
```

## OptionParser

Reads command-line switches into a map.

### OptionParser.parse

```
OptionParser.parse(enum[string], map[string,string]) -> tuple[map[string,string],list[string],list[tuple[string,string]]]
OptionParser.parse(enum[string], map[string,string], map[string,string]) -> tuple[map[string,string],list[string],list[tuple[string,string]]]
OptionParser.parse(enum[string], list[tuple[atom,list[tuple[atom,atom]]]]) -> tuple[list[tuple[atom,string]],list[string],list[tuple[string,option[string]]]]
```

Reads switches from command-line arguments. The second argument maps each switch to its type: boolean, string, integer, float or count; a third maps one-letter aliases to switch names. It returns the values as text by name, the arguments that are not switches, and the switches that are unknown or have a value of the wrong type. --name=value and --name value both work, --no-name sets a boolean to false, dashes in a name become underscores, and -- ends the switches.

```elixir
alx> {options, files, invalid} = OptionParser.parse(["--verbose", "--jobs=4", "a.txt", "--dry-run", "--color", "red", "b.txt"], %{"verbose" => "boolean", "jobs" => "integer", "dry_run" => "boolean"})
alx> options
%{"dry_run" => "true", "jobs" => "4", "verbose" => "true"}
alx> files
["a.txt", "red", "b.txt"]
alx> invalid
[{"--color", ""}]
alx> {short, _, _} = OptionParser.parse(["-v", "-v", "--no-color", "-n", "x"], %{"verbose" => "count", "color" => "boolean", "name" => "string"}, %{"v" => "verbose", "n" => "name"})
alx> short
%{"color" => "false", "name" => "x", "verbose" => "2"}
```

### OptionParser.parse_head

```
OptionParser.parse_head(enum[string], list[tuple[atom,list[tuple[atom,atom]]]]) -> tuple[list[tuple[atom,string]],list[string],list[tuple[string,option[string]]]]
```

Like OptionParser.parse with options, stopping at the first argument that is not a switch.

```elixir
alx> OptionParser.parse_head(["--x", "1", "cmd", "--y"], [strict: [x: :integer]])
{[x: "1"], ["cmd", "--y"], []}
```

### OptionParser.split

```
OptionParser.split(string) -> list[string]
```

Splits a command line into arguments as a shell does: at spaces outside quotes, with backslash escapes.

```elixir
alx> OptionParser.split("a 'b c' \"d e\"")
["a", "b c", "d e"]
```

### OptionParser.to_argv

```
OptionParser.to_argv(list[tuple[atom,string]]) -> list[string]
```

Writes switches back as arguments: --name value, and --name or --no-name for "true" and "false".

```elixir
alx> OptionParser.to_argv([name: "ada", debug: "true", color: "false"])
["--name", "ada", "--debug", "--no-color"]
```

## Logger

Leveled messages on standard error.

### Logger.add_handler

```
Logger.add_handler(atom, fn[atom,string,list[tuple[atom,string]],b]) -> boolean
```

Sends every message that passes the level, with its level and metadata, to a function as well as to the console; false when the name is taken. :console names the console itself, which remove_handler can turn off.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(4)
alx> Logger.add_handler(:doc_handler, fn level, text, _ -> Process.send(me, to_string(level) <> " " <> text, 100) end)
true
alx> Logger.error("handled")
alx> Process.receive(me, 1000)
{true, "error handled"}
alx> Logger.remove_handler(:doc_handler)
true
```

### Logger.configure

```
Logger.configure(string)
Logger.configure(list[tuple[atom,string]])
```

Sets the lowest level that is written: debug, info, warning, error or none. It starts at debug, or at what the ALCHEM_LOG_LEVEL environment variable names.

```elixir
alx> Logger.configure("warning")
alx> Logger.level()
"warning"
alx> Logger.configure("debug")
```

### Logger.debug

```
Logger.debug(string)
Logger.debug(fn[string])
Logger.debug(string, list[tuple[atom,string]])
```

Writes a debug message to standard error, when the level allows it.

```elixir
alx> Logger.debug("cache miss")
```

### Logger.error

```
Logger.error(string)
Logger.error(fn[string])
Logger.error(string, list[tuple[atom,string]])
```

Writes an error message to standard error.

```elixir
alx> Logger.error("connection lost")
```

### Logger.info

```
Logger.info(string)
Logger.info(fn[string])
Logger.info(string, list[tuple[atom,string]])
```

Writes an informational message to standard error as time, level and text.

```elixir
alx> Logger.info("listening on 8080")
```

### Logger.level

```
Logger.level() -> string
```

The lowest level that is currently written.

```elixir
alx> Logger.configure("info")
alx> Logger.level()
"info"
alx> Logger.configure("debug")
```

### Logger.log

```
Logger.log(atom, string)
```

Logs a message at a level given as :debug, :info, :warning or :error.

```elixir
alx> Logger.log(:debug, "from the docs")
```

### Logger.metadata

```
Logger.metadata(list[tuple[atom,string]])
Logger.metadata() -> list[tuple[atom,string]]
```

Adds name: value pairs to the calling process's metadata, which goes with every message it logs; without arguments, the metadata so far.

```elixir
alx> Logger.metadata([request_id: "r1"])
alx> Logger.metadata()
[request_id: "r1"]
```

### Logger.remove_handler

```
Logger.remove_handler(atom) -> boolean
```

Stops sending messages to a handler; false when there is none by that name.

```elixir
alx> Logger.remove_handler(:never_added)
false
```

### Logger.warning

```
Logger.warning(string)
Logger.warning(fn[string])
Logger.warning(string, list[tuple[atom,string]])
```

Writes a warning to standard error.

```elixir
alx> Logger.warning("retrying")
```

## Port

Runs an external program and exchanges text with it: its output arrives as messages, a line at a time.

### Port.close

```
Port.close(port) -> boolean
```

Closes the program's standard input, so a program that reads to the end can finish; false when it was already closed. Stopping the owning process ends the program.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[PortEvent] = Process.self(8)
alx> case Port.open("cat", Enum.take([""], 0), me) do
...>   ok(echo) -> {Port.close(echo), Port.close(echo)}
...>   error(_) -> {false, false}
...> end
{true, false}
alx> assert_receive(me, PortEvent.exit(0), 5000)
```

### Port.command

```
Port.command(port, string) -> boolean
```

Writes text to the program's standard input; false once the port is closed or the program has gone.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[PortEvent] = Process.self(8)
alx> case Port.open("cat", Enum.take([""], 0), me) do
...>   ok(echo) -> Port.command(echo, "hello\n") and Port.close(echo)
...>   error(_) -> false
...> end
true
alx> assert_receive(me, PortEvent.data("hello"), 5000)
```

### Port.info

```
Port.info(port) -> option[Port.Info]
```

What is known about a port's running program: its name, operating system process id and the bytes written to and read from it; none once it has ended.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[PortEvent] = Process.self(8)
alx> ok(port) = Port.open("cat", [], me)
alx> some(info) = Port.info(port)
alx> info.name
"cat"
alx> Port.close(port)
true
```

### Port.monitor

```
Port.monitor(port, pid[PortEvent]) -> boolean
```

Sends the program's exit status to another process too, as PortEvent.exit, when it ends; false when it has already ended.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[PortEvent] = Process.self(8)
alx> ok(port) = Port.open("true", [], me)
alx> Process.receive(me, 5000)
{true, PortEvent.exit(0)}
alx> Port.monitor(port, me)
false
```

### Port.open

```
Port.open(string, enum[string], pid[PortEvent]) -> result[port,string]
Port.open(string, enum[string], pid[PortEvent], list[tuple[atom,atom]]) -> result[port,string]
Port.open(string, enum[string], pid[PortEvent], list[tuple[atom,integer]]) -> result[port,string]
```

Starts an external program with arguments. Each line it writes, to standard output or standard error, is sent to the owner as PortEvent.data(text), and PortEvent.exit(status) follows when it ends. The result is an error when the program cannot be started.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[PortEvent] = Process.self(16)
alx> case Port.open("sort", Enum.take([""], 0), me) do
...>   ok(sorter) ->
...>     Port.command(sorter, "pear\napple\n")
...>     Port.close(sorter)
...>   error(_) -> false
...> end
true
alx> assert_receive(me, PortEvent.data(first), 5000)
alx> first
"apple"
alx> assert_receive(me, PortEvent.data("pear"), 5000)
alx> assert_receive(me, PortEvent.exit(status), 5000)
alx> status
0
alx> case Port.open("alchem-no-such-program", Enum.take([""], 0), me) do
...>   ok(_) -> "started"
...>   error(_) -> "not found"
...> end
"not found"
```

### Port.os_pid

```
Port.os_pid(port) -> integer
```

The operating system's process identifier of the program.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[PortEvent] = Process.self(8)
alx> case Port.open("cat", Enum.take([""], 0), me) do
...>   ok(echo) -> Port.os_pid(echo) > 0 and Port.close(echo)
...>   error(_) -> false
...> end
true
```

## Process

Lightweight processes with typed mailboxes, links and monitors.

### Process.alive

```
Process.alive(pid[t]) -> boolean
```

Reports whether the process is still running.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[integer] = Process.self(1)
alx> Process.alive(me)
true
```

### Process.await

```
Process.await(pid[t], integer) -> tuple[boolean,string]
```

Waits up to the given milliseconds for a process and everything it started to end, returning whether it did and its exit reason.

```elixir
alx> worker: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do 0 end, 1)
alx> Process.await(worker, 1000)
{true, "normal"}
```

### Process.cancel_timer

```
Process.cancel_timer(integer) -> boolean
```

Cancels a timer from Process.send_after or Server.send_after; false when it had already fired or been cancelled.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(4)
alx> timer = Process.send_after(me, "late", 60000)
alx> Process.cancel_timer(timer)
true
alx> Process.cancel_timer(timer)
false
```

### Process.crash

```
Process.crash(string) -> integer
```

Fails the current process with a reason. Typed as integer so a worker can end with it.

```elixir
alx> worker: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.crash("bad input") end, 1)
alx> {ended, reason} = Process.await(worker, 1000)
alx> ended and String.contains?(reason, "bad input")
true
```

### Process.demonitor

```
Process.demonitor(pid[t], integer) -> boolean
```

Cancels a monitor and discards its notification if already queued.

```elixir
alx> worker: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end, 1)
alx> reference = Process.monitor(worker)
alx> Process.demonitor(worker, reference)
true
alx> Process.stop(worker)
true
```

### Process.event

```
Process.event(integer) -> tuple[boolean,integer,integer,string]
```

Waits up to the given milliseconds for a monitor or link notification: {arrived, reference, process_id, reason}. Link events have reference 0.

```elixir
alx> {arrived, _, _, _} = Process.event(1)
alx> arrived
false
```

### Process.id

```
Process.id(pid[t]) -> integer
```

The process's unique positive identifier. Pids are compared by id.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[integer] = Process.self(1)
alx> Process.id(me) > 0
true
```

### Process.link

```
Process.link(pid[t]) -> boolean
```

Links the current process with another: when either fails, the other is stopped too unless it traps exits.

```elixir
alx> Process.trap_exits(true)
alx> worker: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end, 1)
alx> Process.link(worker)
true
alx> Process.unlink(worker)
true
alx> Process.stop(worker)
true
```

### Process.loop

```
Process.loop(s, fn[s,tuple[boolean,s]]) -> s
```

Runs a state loop without growing the stack: the function returns {continue, next_state}, and the final state is returned once continue is false.

```elixir
alx> Process.loop(1, fn(n: integer): tuple[boolean, integer] do {n < 100, n * 2} end)
256
```

### Process.monitor

```
Process.monitor(pid[t]) -> integer
```

Asks to be notified once when the process ends, returning a reference. Process.event receives the notification.

```elixir
alx> worker: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do 0 end, 1)
alx> reference = Process.monitor(worker)
alx> {arrived, noticed, _, reason} = Process.event(1000)
alx> arrived and noticed == reference and reason == "normal"
true
```

### Process.receive

```
Process.receive(pid[t], integer) -> tuple[boolean,t]
```

Takes the next message from the current process's mailbox, waiting up to the given milliseconds. The flag is false on timeout.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[integer] = Process.self(4)
alx> Process.send(me, 7, 100)
true
alx> Process.receive(me, 100)
{true, 7}
alx> {arrived, _} = Process.receive(me, 10)
alx> arrived
false
```

### Process.register

```
Process.register(pid[a], atom) -> boolean
```

Gives a process a name by which this node, and the nodes connected to it, can find it. A name belongs to one living process at a time. The message type must be one that can be copied to another node: no functions, streams or other handles tied to this program.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(4)
alx> Process.register(me, :doc_register)
true
alx> Process.register(me, :doc_register)
false
alx> Process.unregister(:doc_register)
true
```

### Process.report

```
Process.report(pid[t]) -> string
```

Where and why a process failed, or its exit reason; meaningful once it has ended.

```elixir
alx> worker: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.crash("bad input") end, 1)
alx> Process.await(worker, 1000)
alx> String.contains?(Process.report(worker), "bad input")
true
```

### Process.self

```
Process.self(integer) -> pid[t]
```

The current process, creating its mailbox with the given capacity on first use. The message type comes from the annotation.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(8)
alx> Process.send(me, "hello", 100)
true
alx> Process.receive(me, 100)
{true, "hello"}
```

### Process.send

```
Process.send(pid[t], t, integer) -> boolean
```

Queues a message for a process, waiting up to the given milliseconds for room. False when it timed out or the process has ended.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[integer] = Process.self(4)
alx> Process.send(me, 7, 100)
true
```

### Process.send_after

```
Process.send_after(atom, a, integer) -> integer
Process.send_after(pid[a], a, integer) -> integer
```

Sends a message to a process after the given milliseconds and returns a timer reference for Process.cancel_timer. A message to a process that has ended by then is dropped. Given a name instead of a pid, the message goes to whatever holds the name when the time comes: a process registered with Process.register whose messages are of the message's type, or a server registered with Server.register whose requests are, as a cast; when nothing fitting holds it, the message is dropped.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(4)
alx> timer = Process.send_after(me, "ping", 10)
alx> timer > 0
true
alx> Process.receive(me, 1000)
{true, "ping"}
alx> Process.register(me, :doc_inbox)
true
alx> Process.send_after(:doc_inbox, "named", 10) > 0
true
alx> Process.receive(me, 1000)
{true, "named"}
alx> Process.unregister(:doc_inbox)
true
```

### Process.sleep

```
Process.sleep(integer) -> integer
```

Pauses the current process for a number of milliseconds and returns 0. Process.sleep(0) yields to other processes.

```elixir
alx> Process.sleep(1)
0
```

### Process.spawn

```
Process.spawn(fn[pid[t],integer], integer) -> pid[t]
```

Starts a process running the function, which receives its own pid and returns an exit status. The second argument is the mailbox capacity.

```elixir
alx> parent: pid[integer] = Process.self(8)
alx> worker: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do
...>   {_, n} = Process.receive(self, 1000)
...>   Process.send(parent, n * 2, 1000)
...>   0
...> end, 8)
alx> Process.send(worker, 21, 1000)
true
alx> Process.receive(parent, 1000)
{true, 42}
```

### Process.stop

```
Process.stop(pid[t]) -> boolean
```

Asks a process to stop; true when this request was the first.

```elixir
alx> worker: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end, 1)
alx> Process.stop(worker)
true
alx> {ended, _} = Process.await(worker, 1000)
alx> ended
true
```

### Process.trap_exits

```
Process.trap_exits(boolean) -> boolean
```

Chooses whether linked failures arrive as events instead of stopping this process, returning the previous setting.

```elixir
alx> Process.trap_exits(true)
alx> Process.trap_exits(false)
true
```

### Process.unlink

```
Process.unlink(pid[t]) -> boolean
```

Removes a link in both directions; true when there was one.

```elixir
alx> worker: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end, 1)
alx> Process.unlink(worker)
false
alx> Process.stop(worker)
true
```

### Process.unregister

```
Process.unregister(atom) -> boolean
```

Frees a name; false when it was not registered.

```elixir
alx> Process.unregister(:doc_nobody)
false
```

### Process.whereis

```
Process.whereis(atom) -> option[pid[a]]
```

Finds a process of this node by name. The message type comes from the annotation and must be the one the name was registered with.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[integer] = Process.self(4)
alx> Process.register(me, :doc_whereis)
true
alx> found: option[pid[integer]] = Process.whereis(:doc_whereis)
alx> case found do
...>   some(named) -> Process.send(named, 7, 100)
...>   none -> false
...> end
true
alx> assert_receive(me, 7)
alx> other: option[pid[string]] = Process.whereis(:doc_whereis)
alx> case other do
...>   some(_) -> "found"
...>   none -> "registered for another type"
...> end
"registered for another type"
```

## Node

Connects this program to others so that their processes can exchange messages, which are copied between them.

### Node.address

```
Node.address() -> string
```

The address this node listens at, with the port that was picked.

```elixir
alx> Node.start("docs", "127.0.0.1:0", "secret")
alx> String.starts_with?(Node.address(), "127.0.0.1:")
true
```

### Node.call

```
Node.call(string, atom, a) -> result[b,string]
Node.call(string, atom, a, integer) -> result[b,string]
```

Runs a function a node serves and returns its result: ok(value), or error(reason) when it failed, nothing is served under the name, or no answer came within 5 seconds or the given milliseconds. The result's type comes from the annotation.

```elixir
alx> Node.serve(:square_doc, fn(n: integer): integer do n * n end)
true
alx> squared: result[integer, string] = Node.call(Node.self(), :square_doc, 7)
alx> squared
ok(49)
```

### Node.cast

```
Node.cast(string, atom, a) -> boolean
```

Runs a function a node serves without waiting for it, whatever the function returns. On this node it reports whether the name is served; a cast to another node is true once it is on its way, and is dropped if that node serves nothing under the name.

```elixir
alx> Node.serve(:noted_doc, fn(n: integer): integer do n end)
true
alx> Node.cast(Node.self(), :noted_doc, 1)
true
```

### Node.connect

```
Node.connect(string) -> result[string,string]
Node.connect(string, list[tuple[atom,boolean]]) -> result[string,string]
```

Connects to the node listening at an address and returns its name. Both nodes must have the same cookie. Messages to its processes are then copied over the connection.

```elixir
alx> Node.start("docs", "127.0.0.1:0", "secret")
alx> case Node.connect("127.0.0.1:1") do
...>   ok(name) -> name
...>   error(_) -> "not reachable"
...> end
"not reachable"
```

### Node.disconnect

```
Node.disconnect(string) -> boolean
```

Closes the connection to a node; false when there is none.

```elixir
alx> Node.disconnect("nobody")
false
```

### Node.list

```
Node.list() -> list[string]
```

The names of the nodes this one is connected to, in order.

```elixir
alx> length(Node.list())
0
```

### Node.monitor

```
Node.monitor(string) -> integer
```

Asks for one event when the connection to a node ends, read with Process.event: its reason is "nodedown" and the node's name. A node that is not connected produces the event at once.

```elixir
alx> reference = Node.monitor("elsewhere")
alx> {arrived, noticed, _, reason} = Process.event(1000)
alx> arrived and noticed == reference and reason == "nodedown elsewhere"
true
```

### Node.register_global

```
Node.register_global(pid[a], atom) -> boolean
```

Registers a process under a name that no connected node has for the same message type, so that any of them finds it with whereis_global; false when one has.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(4)
alx> Node.register_global(me, :global_doc)
true
alx> Node.register_global(me, :global_doc)
false
```

### Node.self

```
Node.self() -> string
```

This node's name, or "" before Node.start.

```elixir
alx> Node.start("docs", "127.0.0.1:0", "secret")
alx> Node.self()
"docs"
```

### Node.serve

```
Node.serve(atom, fn[a,b]) -> boolean
```

Offers a function to other nodes under a name, for Node.call and Node.cast: each call runs it in a process of its own, and a failure is returned to the caller as error(reason). Its argument and result must be able to cross between nodes.

```elixir
alx> Node.serve(:twice_doc, fn(n: integer): integer do n * 2 end)
true
```

### Node.start

```
Node.start(string, string) -> result[tuple[],string]
Node.start(string, string, string) -> result[tuple[],string]
Node.start(string, string, string, list[tuple[atom,boolean]]) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Makes this program a node: it listens at the address for other nodes, under a name, and accepts those that know the same cookie. Port 0 picks a free port. With two arguments the cookie comes from the ALCHEM_COOKIE environment variable. Connections are encrypted; a fourth argument, [encrypted: false], turns that off for a trusted network, and only nodes with the same setting connect. A program becomes a node once.

```elixir
alx> started = Node.start("docs", "127.0.0.1:0", "secret")
alx> started == ok({}) or started == error("this program is already a node")
true
alx> Node.self()
"docs"
alx> Node.start("docs", "127.0.0.1:0", "secret", [loud: true])
error("unknown option :loud; Node.start takes encrypted:")
```

### Node.stream

```
Node.stream(string, atom) -> result[stream[a],string]
```

Finds a stream another node has published and returns one that pulls from it, a chunk at a time, as it is consumed. The element type comes from the annotation and must be the one published. An endless stream can be read from; a reader that stops early pulls no more. Reading fails if the other node stops answering.

```elixir
alx> Node.start("docs", "127.0.0.1:0", "secret")
alx> squares: result[stream[integer], string] = Node.stream("elsewhere", :doc_squares)
alx> case squares do
...>   ok(found) -> Enum.take(found, 3)
...>   error(_) -> Enum.take([0], 0)
...> end
Enum.take([0], 0)
```

### Node.whereis

```
Node.whereis(string, atom) -> option[pid[a]]
Node.whereis(string, atom, integer) -> option[pid[a]]
```

Finds a process another node has registered under a name, waiting up to 5 seconds or the given milliseconds. The message type comes from the annotation and must be the type the name was registered with. The handle can be sent to and put in messages; receiving, monitoring and linking need a process of this node.

```elixir
alx> Node.start("docs", "127.0.0.1:0", "secret")
alx> found: option[pid[string]] = Node.whereis("elsewhere", :logger, 100)
alx> case found do
...>   some(logger) -> Process.send(logger, "hello", 100)
...>   none -> false
...> end
false
```

### Node.whereis_global

```
Node.whereis_global(atom) -> option[pid[a]]
```

Finds a process registered under a name on this node or any connected one. The message type comes from the annotation.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(4)
alx> Node.register_global(me, :global_find_doc)
true
alx> found: option[pid[string]] = Node.whereis_global(:global_find_doc)
alx> case found do
...>   some(_) -> "found"
...>   none -> "missing"
...> end
"found"
```

## Supervisor

Restarts child processes according to a strategy.

### Supervisor.alive

```
Supervisor.alive(supervisor[t]) -> boolean
```

Reports whether the supervisor is running.

```elixir
alx> group = Supervisor.start("one_for_one", 3, 1000, [{"worker", "permanent", fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end}], 4)
alx> Supervisor.stop(group, 1000)
true
alx> Supervisor.alive(group)
false
```

### Supervisor.await

```
Supervisor.await(supervisor[t], integer) -> tuple[boolean,string]
```

Waits up to the given milliseconds for the supervisor to end, returning whether it did and why.

```elixir
alx> group = Supervisor.start("one_for_one", 3, 1000, [{"worker", "permanent", fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end}], 4)
alx> Supervisor.stop(group, 1000)
true
alx> {ended, _} = Supervisor.await(group, 1000)
alx> ended
true
```

### Supervisor.child

```
Supervisor.child(supervisor[t], string) -> pid[t]
```

The current pid of a named child, for sending it messages.

```elixir
alx> group = Supervisor.start("one_for_one", 3, 1000, [{"worker", "permanent", fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end}], 4)
alx> Process.alive(Supervisor.child(group, "worker"))
true
alx> Supervisor.stop(group, 1000)
true
```

### Supervisor.children

```
Supervisor.children(supervisor[t]) -> list[tuple[string,integer]]
```

Each child's name with its current process id, in declaration order.

```elixir
alx> group = Supervisor.start("one_for_one", 3, 1000, [{"worker", "permanent", fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end}], 4)
alx> Enum.map(Supervisor.children(group), fn {name, _} -> name end)
["worker"]
alx> Supervisor.stop(group, 1000)
true
```

### Supervisor.restarts

```
Supervisor.restarts(supervisor[t]) -> integer
```

How many restarts the supervisor has performed.

```elixir
alx> group = Supervisor.start("one_for_one", 3, 1000, [{"worker", "permanent", fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end}], 4)
alx> Supervisor.restarts(group)
0
alx> Supervisor.stop(group, 1000)
true
```

### Supervisor.server

```
Supervisor.server(atom, string, s, fn[s,q,tuple[s,r]]) -> tuple[string,string,fn[pid[tuple[]],integer]]
```

A child for Supervisor.start that runs a server under a name: the child registers the server, Supervisor.start returns once it has, and Server.whereis finds whichever server is running. A failing server makes its child fail, so the strategy and the policy ("permanent", "transient" or "temporary") decide the restart, which begins from the initial state. Servers of different types can share one supervisor.

```elixir
alx> tree = Supervisor.start("one_for_one", 3, 1000, [Supervisor.server(:doc_total, "permanent", 0, fn(total: integer, n: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + n, total + n} end)], 1)
alx> found: option[server[integer, integer]] = Server.whereis(:doc_total)
alx> case found do
...>   some(total) -> Server.call(total, 5, 1000)
...>   none -> error("not found")
...> end
ok(5)
alx> Supervisor.stop(tree, 1000)
true
```

### Supervisor.start

```
Supervisor.start(string, integer, integer, list[tuple[string,string,fn[pid[t],integer]]], integer) -> supervisor[t]
```

Starts children under a strategy ("one_for_one", "one_for_all" or "rest_for_one"), giving up after max_restarts within window_ms. Each child is {name, restart_policy, function}, with policy "permanent", "transient" or "temporary"; the last argument is each child's mailbox capacity.

```elixir
alx> group = Supervisor.start("one_for_one", 3, 1000, [{"worker", "permanent", fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end}], 4)
alx> Supervisor.alive(group)
true
alx> Supervisor.stop(group, 1000)
true
```

### Supervisor.start_link

```
Supervisor.start_link(string, integer, integer, list[tuple[string,string,fn[pid[t],integer]]], integer) -> supervisor[t]
```

Like Supervisor.start, and also links the supervisor to the process starting it.

```elixir
alx> group = Supervisor.start_link("one_for_one", 3, 1000, [{"worker", "permanent", fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end}], 4)
alx> Supervisor.stop(group, 1000)
true
```

### Supervisor.stop

```
Supervisor.stop(supervisor[t], integer) -> boolean
```

Stops the supervisor and its children, waiting up to the given milliseconds; false when the wait ran out.

```elixir
alx> group = Supervisor.start("one_for_one", 3, 1000, [{"worker", "permanent", fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do Process.sleep(60000) end}], 4)
alx> Supervisor.stop(group, 1000)
true
```

## Server

A process owning a state that answers typed requests in order.

### Server.alive

```
Server.alive(server[q,r]) -> boolean
```

Reports whether the server is running.

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end)
alx> Server.alive(counter)
true
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
```

### Server.await

```
Server.await(server[q,r], integer) -> tuple[boolean,string]
```

Waits up to the given milliseconds for the server to end, returning whether it did and its exit reason.

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end)
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
alx> {ended, _} = Server.await(counter, 1000)
alx> ended
true
```

### Server.call

```
Server.call(server[q,r], q, integer) -> result[r,string]
```

Sends a request and waits up to the given milliseconds for the reply: ok(reply), or error("timeout"), error("server is not running") or error("server stopped: reason").

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end)
alx> Server.call(counter, 5, 1000)
ok(5)
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
```

### Server.cast

```
Server.cast(server[q,r], q) -> boolean
```

Queues a request without waiting for the reply; false when the server has stopped or its queue is full.

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end)
alx> Server.cast(counter, 5)
true
alx> Server.call(counter, 0, 1000)
ok(5)
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
```

### Server.continue

```
Server.continue(q) -> boolean
```

Asks the running server to handle a request of its own as soon as it has answered the current one, ahead of any request already waiting: the work a handler defers until after its reply, as handle_continue does in Elixir. Replies to continued requests go nowhere.

```elixir
alx> loader = Server.start([], fn(steps: list[string], step: string): tuple[list[string], list[string]] do
...>   if step == "start" do
...>     Server.continue("load")
...>   end
...>   {steps ++ [step], steps ++ [step]}
...> end)
alx> Server.call(loader, "start", 1000)
ok(["start"])
alx> Server.call(loader, "check", 1000)
ok(["start", "load", "check"])
alx> Server.stop(loader)
true
```

### Server.mailbox

```
Server.mailbox(server[q,r], fn[m,q]) -> pid[m]
```

Gives a server a pid that any process, port or socket can send to. Each message becomes a request, made from the message inside the server by the function and queued like a cast: the messages Elixir delivers to handle_info. The mailbox ends with the server; for a supervised server it outlives restarts.

```elixir
alx> log = Server.start([], fn(seen: list[string], event: string): tuple[list[string], list[string]] do {seen ++ [event], seen ++ [event]} end)
alx> inbox: pid[integer] = Server.mailbox(log, fn n -> "got " <> to_string(n) end)
alx> Process.send(inbox, 7, 1000)
true
alx> Process.sleep(50)
alx> Server.call(log, "checked", 1000)
ok(["got 7", "checked"])
alx> Server.stop(log)
true
```

### Server.monitor

```
Server.monitor(server[q,r], pid[a], fn[string,q]) -> boolean
```

Turns a process's exit into a request to a server: when the process ends, the function makes a request from the exit reason, inside the server, and it is queued like a cast. This is how a server hears of the processes it depends on.

```elixir
alx> log = Server.start([], fn(seen: list[string], event: string): tuple[list[string], list[string]] do {[event] ++ seen, [event] ++ seen} end)
alx> worker: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do 0 end, 1)
alx> Server.monitor(log, worker, fn reason -> "worker ended: " <> reason end)
true
alx> Process.sleep(50)
alx> Server.call(log, "checked", 1000)
ok(["checked", "worker ended: normal"])
alx> Server.stop(log)
true
```

### Server.register

```
Server.register(server[q,r], atom) -> boolean
```

Gives a server a name that Server.whereis finds. A name belongs to one living process or server at a time; a supervised server keeps its name across restarts. Process.unregister frees it.

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end)
alx> Server.register(counter, :doc_counter)
true
alx> Server.register(counter, :doc_counter)
false
alx> Process.unregister(:doc_counter)
true
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
```

### Server.restarts

```
Server.restarts(server[q,r]) -> integer
```

How many times a supervised server has been restarted; 0 for an unsupervised one.

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end)
alx> Server.restarts(counter)
0
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
```

### Server.self

```
Server.self() -> server[q,r]
```

The server whose handler is running, for a handler that schedules requests for itself or gives its handle away. The request and reply types come from the annotation and must be the server's own.

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do
...>   me: server[integer, integer] = Server.self()
...>   if amount > 1 do
...>     Server.cast(me, amount - 1)
...>   end
...>   {total + amount, total + amount}
...> end)
alx> Server.cast(counter, 3)
true
alx> Process.sleep(50)
alx> Server.call(counter, 0, 1000)
ok(6)
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
```

### Server.send_after

```
Server.send_after(server[q,r], q, integer) -> integer
```

Casts a request to a server after the given milliseconds and returns a timer reference for Process.cancel_timer. A server can schedule work for itself with Server.self.

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end)
alx> Server.send_after(counter, 5, 10) > 0
true
alx> Process.sleep(100)
alx> Server.call(counter, 0, 1000)
ok(5)
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
```

### Server.start

```
Server.start(s, fn[s,q,tuple[s,r]]) -> server[q,r]
```

Starts a process owning a state. The handler takes the state and a request and returns {next_state, reply}; requests are answered one at a time, in order.

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end)
alx> Server.call(counter, 5, 1000)
ok(5)
alx> Server.call(counter, 2, 1000)
ok(7)
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
```

### Server.start_supervised

```
Server.start_supervised(s, fn[s,q,tuple[s,r]], integer, integer) -> server[q,r]
```

Like Server.start, restarting the server with its initial state when the handler fails, up to max_restarts within window_ms.

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start_supervised(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end, 3, 1000)
alx> Server.call(counter, 5, 1000)
ok(5)
alx> Server.restarts(counter)
0
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
```

### Server.stop

```
Server.stop(server[q,r]) -> boolean
```

Asks the server to shut down.

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end)
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
```

### Server.whereis

```
Server.whereis(atom) -> option[server[q,r]]
```

Finds a server by name. The request and reply types come from the annotation; a name registered for other types, or for a process, is not found.

```elixir
alx> counter = Server.start(0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end)
alx> Server.register(counter, :doc_named)
true
alx> found: option[server[integer, integer]] = Server.whereis(:doc_named)
alx> case found do
...>   some(named) -> Server.call(named, 4, 1000)
...>   none -> error("missing")
...> end
ok(4)
alx> other: option[server[string, string]] = Server.whereis(:doc_named)
alx> case other do
...>   some(_) -> "found"
...>   none -> "not found"
...> end
"not found"
alx> Server.stop(counter)
true
```

## Task

Runs a function in its own process and collects its result.

### Task.async

```
Task.async(fn[a]) -> task[a]
```

Runs the function in its own process, linked to the caller, and returns a task to await. A task that fails takes its caller with it, unless the caller traps exits; Task.Supervisor.async_nolink starts one that does not.

```elixir
alx> task = Task.async(fn -> 6 * 7 end)
alx> Task.await(task)
42
```

### Task.async_stream

```
Task.async_stream(enum[a], fn[a,b]) -> stream[b]
Task.async_stream(enum[a], fn[a,b], integer) -> stream[b]
```

Runs the function over each element concurrently, at most one task per processor (or the given number) at a time, yielding results in input order.

```elixir
alx> Task.async_stream([1, 2, 3], fn n -> n * n end) |> Enum.to_list()
[1, 4, 9]
alx> Task.async_stream(1..4, fn n -> n + 1 end, 2) |> Enum.sum()
14
```

### Task.await

```
Task.await(task[a]) -> a
Task.await(task[a], integer) -> a
```

Waits for a task's result, for 5 seconds or the given milliseconds. Fails the caller when the task failed or the time ran out.

```elixir
alx> Task.await(Task.async(fn -> "done" end), 1000)
"done"
```

### Task.await_many

```
Task.await_many(enum[task[a]]) -> list[a]
Task.await_many(enum[task[a]], integer) -> list[a]
```

Waits for every task, returning the results in order.

```elixir
alx> Task.await_many([Task.async(fn -> 1 end), Task.async(fn -> 2 end)])
[1, 2]
```

### Task.shutdown

```
Task.shutdown(task[a]) -> boolean
```

Stops a task whose result is no longer wanted.

```elixir
alx> task = Task.async(fn -> Process.sleep(60000) end)
alx> Task.shutdown(task)
true
```

### Task.start

```
Task.start(fn[a]) -> task[a]
```

Runs the function in its own process, not linked to the caller, for work nobody needs to wait for; the task can still be awaited or shut down.

```elixir
alx> task = Task.start(fn -> 5 end)
alx> Task.await(task)
5
```

### Task.start_link

```
Task.start_link(fn[a]) -> task[a]
```

Like Task.start, linked to the caller: a task that fails takes the caller with it.

```elixir
alx> task = Task.start_link(fn -> 8 end)
alx> Task.await(task, 1000)
8
```

### Task.yield

```
Task.yield(task[a], integer) -> option[result[a,string]]
```

Waits up to the given milliseconds: some(ok(value)) when the task finished, some(error(reason)) when it failed, none when it is still running.

```elixir
alx> Task.yield(Task.async(fn -> 42 end), 1000)
some(ok(42))
alx> slow = Task.async(fn -> Process.sleep(60000) end)
alx> Task.yield(slow, 1)
none
alx> Task.shutdown(slow)
true
```

## Task.Supervisor

Runs tasks as temporary children of a supervisor: a task supervisor is a dynamic_supervisor, so DynamicSupervisor's functions apply to it too.

### Task.Supervisor.async

```
Task.Supervisor.async(dynamic_supervisor, fn[a]) -> task[a]
```

Runs the function as a task under the supervisor, linked to the caller, and returns it to await.

```elixir
alx> tasks = Task.Supervisor.start_link()
alx> Task.await(Task.Supervisor.async(tasks, fn -> 6 * 7 end))
42
```

### Task.Supervisor.async_nolink

```
Task.Supervisor.async_nolink(dynamic_supervisor, fn[a]) -> task[a]
```

Runs the function as a task under the supervisor, not linked to the caller: a failure is seen only by awaiting or yielding the task.

```elixir
alx> tasks = Task.Supervisor.start_link()
alx> task = Task.Supervisor.async_nolink(tasks, fn -> div(1, 0) end)
alx> case Task.yield(task, 1000) do
...>   some(error(_)) -> "failed"
...>   _ -> "other"
...> end
"failed"
```

### Task.Supervisor.children

```
Task.Supervisor.children(dynamic_supervisor) -> list[integer]
```

The process ids of the supervisor's running tasks.

```elixir
alx> tasks = Task.Supervisor.start_link()
alx> ok(_) = Task.Supervisor.start_child(tasks, fn -> Process.sleep(60000) end)
alx> length(Task.Supervisor.children(tasks))
1
alx> DynamicSupervisor.stop(tasks)
true
```

### Task.Supervisor.start_child

```
Task.Supervisor.start_child(dynamic_supervisor, fn[a]) -> result[task[a],string]
```

Starts a task under the supervisor that nobody needs to await, unlinked: ok(task), or error("max_children") or error("supervisor is not running").

```elixir
alx> tasks = Task.Supervisor.start_link()
alx> ok(task) = Task.Supervisor.start_child(tasks, fn -> 1 end)
alx> Task.await(task)
1
```

### Task.Supervisor.start_link

```
Task.Supervisor.start_link() -> dynamic_supervisor
Task.Supervisor.start_link(list[tuple[atom,integer]]) -> dynamic_supervisor
```

Starts a task supervisor, with DynamicSupervisor's options such as max_children:.

```elixir
alx> tasks = Task.Supervisor.start_link()
alx> Task.Supervisor.children(tasks)
[]
alx> limited = Task.Supervisor.start_link([max_children: 4])
alx> DynamicSupervisor.stop(limited)
true
```

### Task.Supervisor.terminate_child

```
Task.Supervisor.terminate_child(dynamic_supervisor, task[a]) -> boolean
```

Stops one of the supervisor's tasks; false when it is not running there.

```elixir
alx> tasks = Task.Supervisor.start_link()
alx> ok(task) = Task.Supervisor.start_child(tasks, fn -> Process.sleep(60000) end)
alx> Task.Supervisor.terminate_child(tasks, task)
true
alx> Task.Supervisor.terminate_child(tasks, task)
false
```

## Agent

A process holding a state that functions read and update.

### Agent.cast

```
Agent.cast(atom, fn[s,s]) -> boolean
Agent.cast(agent[s], fn[s,s]) -> boolean
```

Queues a state update without waiting for it; false when the agent has stopped.

```elixir
alx> counter = Agent.start(fn -> 0 end)
alx> Agent.cast(counter, fn n -> n + 1 end)
true
alx> Agent.get(counter, fn n -> n end)
1
alx> Agent.stop(counter)
true
```

### Agent.get

```
Agent.get(atom, fn[s,r]) -> r
Agent.get(agent[s], fn[s,r]) -> r
Agent.get(agent[s], fn[s,r], integer) -> r
```

Runs the function on the state inside the agent and returns its result. A last argument waits that many milliseconds instead of 5 seconds.

```elixir
alx> counter = Agent.start(fn -> 41 end)
alx> Agent.get(counter, fn n -> n + 1 end)
42
alx> Agent.stop(counter)
true
```

### Agent.get_and_update

```
Agent.get_and_update(atom, fn[s,tuple[r,s]]) -> r
Agent.get_and_update(agent[s], fn[s,tuple[r,s]]) -> r
Agent.get_and_update(agent[s], fn[s,tuple[r,s]], integer) -> r
```

The function returns {reply, next_state}: one step that reads and changes the state.

```elixir
alx> counter = Agent.start(fn -> 10 end)
alx> Agent.get_and_update(counter, fn n -> {n, n + 1} end)
10
alx> Agent.get(counter, fn n -> n end)
11
alx> Agent.stop(counter)
true
```

### Agent.start

```
Agent.start(fn[s]) -> agent[s]
Agent.start(fn[s], list[tuple[atom,atom]]) -> agent[s]
```

Starts a process holding the state the function returns.

```elixir
alx> counter = Agent.start(fn -> 0 end)
alx> Agent.get(counter, fn n -> n end)
0
alx> Agent.stop(counter)
true
```

### Agent.start_link

```
Agent.start_link(fn[s]) -> agent[s]
Agent.start_link(fn[s], list[tuple[atom,atom]]) -> agent[s]
```

Like Agent.start, and also links the agent to the process starting it. With [name: :name] the agent is registered under the name, and the functions that take an agent also take the name; the state's type then comes from the function's annotation.

```elixir
alx> names = Agent.start_link(fn -> ["ada"] end)
alx> Agent.get(names, &length(&1))
1
alx> Agent.stop(names)
true
alx> Agent.start_link(fn -> 1 end, [name: :doc_agent])
alx> Agent.get(:doc_agent, fn(n: integer): integer do n + 1 end)
2
```

### Agent.stop

```
Agent.stop(agent[s]) -> boolean
```

Stops the agent.

```elixir
alx> counter = Agent.start(fn -> 0 end)
alx> Agent.stop(counter)
true
```

### Agent.update

```
Agent.update(atom, fn[s,s])
Agent.update(agent[s], fn[s,s])
Agent.update(agent[s], fn[s,s], integer)
```

Replaces the state with the function's result, waiting until it is done.

```elixir
alx> counter = Agent.start(fn -> 0 end)
alx> Agent.update(counter, fn n -> n + 5 end)
alx> Agent.get(counter, fn n -> n end)
5
alx> Agent.stop(counter)
true
```

### Agent.whereis

```
Agent.whereis(atom) -> option[agent[s]]
```

Finds an agent by name. The state's type comes from the annotation; a name registered for another type is not found.

```elixir
alx> Agent.start(fn -> 3 end, [name: :doc_found])
alx> found: option[agent[integer]] = Agent.whereis(:doc_found)
alx> case found do
...>   some(agent) -> Agent.get(agent, fn n -> n end)
...>   none -> 0
...> end
3
```

## Testing

Assertions for test files, called without a module name.

### assert

```
assert(boolean)
```

Fails the test, or the program, when the condition is false. A failed comparison reports both sides.

```elixir
alx> assert(1 + 1 == 2)
alx> assert("a" in ["a", "b"])
```

### assert_in_delta

```
assert_in_delta(float, float, float)
```

Fails unless two floats differ by at most the delta.

```elixir
alx> assert_in_delta(0.1 + 0.2, 0.3, 0.0001)
```

### assert_raise

```
assert_raise(string, fn[a])
```

Fails unless the function raises with a message containing the text.

```elixir
alx> assert_raise("division by zero", fn -> div(1, 0) end)
```

### assert_receive

```
assert_receive(pid[t], pattern)
assert_receive(pid[t], pattern, integer)
assert_receive(pid[t], pattern, integer, string)
```

A statement that takes the first message in the current process's mailbox matching a pattern, waiting for one to arrive: 100 milliseconds unless --receive-timeout or a third argument says otherwise. Other messages stay in the mailbox in their order. Names in the pattern are bound for the rest of the test, ^name compares with an existing binding, and when adds a guard. A failure shows the pattern, the values of pinned names and the last ten messages in the mailbox; a fourth argument replaces its first line.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[tuple[string, integer]] = Process.self(8)
alx> Process.send(me, {"started", 1}, 100)
true
alx> Process.send(me, {"finished", 42}, 100)
true
alx> assert_receive(me, {"finished", result})
alx> result
42
alx> assert_receive(me, {_, count} when count < 10, 500, "the start was never reported")
alx> count
1
```

### assert_received

```
assert_received(pid[t], pattern)
assert_received(pid[t], pattern, string)
```

Like assert_receive, but looks only at messages that have already arrived and does not wait. An argument after the pattern replaces the first line of the failure.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[integer] = Process.self(4)
alx> Process.send(me, 7, 100)
true
alx> assert_received(me, n when n > 5)
alx> n
7
```

### capture_io

```
capture_io(fn[a]) -> string
```

Runs the function and returns what was written to standard output meanwhile.

```elixir
alx> capture_io(fn -> IO.puts("hello") end)
"hello\n"
```

### flunk

```
flunk(string)
```

Fails the test with a message.

```elixir
alx> assert_raise("not reached", fn -> flunk("not reached") end)
```

### on_exit

```
on_exit(fn[a])
```

Registers a function to run when the current test ends, whether it passed or failed; several run last first. A failure in one fails the test.

```elixir
alx> File.write!("doc_on_exit.txt", "temporary")
alx> on_exit(fn -> File.rm!("doc_on_exit.txt") end)
alx> File.exists?("doc_on_exit.txt")
true
```

### refute

```
refute(boolean)
```

Fails when the condition is true.

```elixir
alx> refute(1 > 2)
```

### refute_receive

```
refute_receive(pid[t], pattern)
refute_receive(pid[t], pattern, integer)
refute_receive(pid[t], pattern, integer, string)
```

A statement that fails if a message matching the pattern is in the current process's mailbox, or arrives within the wait. Use _ for any message. The arguments after the pattern are those of assert_receive.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(4)
alx> Process.send(me, "ok", 100)
true
alx> refute_receive(me, "error", 10)
alx> assert_receive(me, "ok")
alx> refute_receive(me, _, 10)
```

### refute_received

```
refute_received(pid[t], pattern)
refute_received(pid[t], pattern, string)
```

Like refute_receive, but looks only at messages that have already arrived and does not wait.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[integer] = Process.self(4)
alx> refute_received(me, _)
alx> Process.send(me, 7, 100)
true
alx> refute_received(me, 8, "an eight arrived")
```

## Gen

Generators of random values for check all properties. Values grow with each run, and a failing value shrinks to the smallest that still fails.

### Gen.bind

```
Gen.bind(generator[a], fn[a,generator[b]]) -> generator[b]
```

A generator chosen from each value of another: the second may depend on the first. check all does this for each generator after the first.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.bind(Gen.integer(0, 3), fn n -> Gen.list_of(Gen.constant(n), n, n) end), 10), fn l -> Enum.all?(l, fn n -> n == length(l) end) end)
true
```

### Gen.boolean

```
Gen.boolean() -> generator[boolean]
```

true or false, shrinking to false.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.boolean(), 10), fn b -> b or not b end)
true
```

### Gen.check

```
Gen.check(generator[a], fn[a,b])
Gen.check(generator[a], fn[a,b], integer)
```

Runs the function on generated values, 100 or the given number of times, and fails with the smallest failing value, shrunk, when it fails. check all is the usual way to write it.

```elixir
alx> Gen.check(Gen.integer(), fn n -> assert(n + 0 == n) end, 20)
```

### Gen.constant

```
Gen.constant(a) -> generator[a]
```

Always the same value.

```elixir
alx> Gen.sample(Gen.constant(7), 3)
[7, 7, 7]
```

### Gen.filter

```
Gen.filter(generator[a], fn[a,boolean]) -> generator[a]
```

The generator's values that pass the test; generating 100 in a row that fail it is an error, so filter out few.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.filter(Gen.integer(), fn n -> n != 0 end), 10), fn n -> n != 0 end)
true
```

### Gen.float

```
Gen.float() -> generator[float]
```

Floats between -size and size, shrinking toward 0.

```elixir
alx> length(Gen.sample(Gen.float(), 5))
5
```

### Gen.integer

```
Gen.integer() -> generator[integer]
Gen.integer(integer, integer) -> generator[integer]
```

Integers: without bounds, between -size and size as the runs grow; with bounds, from low to high. Shrinks toward 0, or the bound nearest it.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.integer(1, 6), 20), fn n -> n >= 1 and n <= 6 end)
true
```

### Gen.list_of

```
Gen.list_of(generator[a]) -> generator[list[a]]
Gen.list_of(generator[a], integer, integer) -> generator[list[a]]
```

Lists of the generator's values, up to size long or from min to max long. Shrinks by leaving elements out, then by shrinking them.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.list_of(Gen.boolean(), 2, 3), 10), fn l -> length(l) >= 2 and length(l) <= 3 end)
true
```

### Gen.map

```
Gen.map(generator[a], fn[a,b]) -> generator[b]
```

The generator's values changed by the function.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.map(Gen.integer(), fn n -> n * 2 end), 10), fn n -> rem(n, 2) == 0 end)
true
```

### Gen.map_of

```
Gen.map_of(generator[k], generator[v]) -> generator[map[k,v]]
```

Maps with generated keys and values.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.map_of(Gen.integer(1, 3), Gen.boolean()), 10), fn m -> map_size(m) <= 3 end)
true
```

### Gen.member_of

```
Gen.member_of(enum[a]) -> generator[a]
```

One of the given values, shrinking toward the first.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.member_of([:red, :green]), 10), fn c -> c in [:red, :green] end)
true
```

### Gen.one_of

```
Gen.one_of(list[generator[a]]) -> generator[a]
```

A value of one of the generators, chosen at random.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.one_of([Gen.constant(0), Gen.integer(10, 20)]), 10), fn n -> n == 0 or n >= 10 end)
true
```

### Gen.positive_integer

```
Gen.positive_integer() -> generator[integer]
```

Integers from 1, shrinking toward 1.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.positive_integer(), 20), fn n -> n >= 1 end)
true
```

### Gen.resize

```
Gen.resize(generator[a], integer) -> generator[a]
```

The generator with its size fixed: Gen.resize(Gen.integer(), 3) stays between -3 and 3.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.resize(Gen.integer(), 3), 20), fn n -> n >= -3 and n <= 3 end)
true
```

### Gen.sample

```
Gen.sample(generator[a], integer) -> list[a]
```

That many values of a generator, growing in size, to see what it makes.

```elixir
alx> length(Gen.sample(Gen.integer(), 4))
4
```

### Gen.string

```
Gen.string(atom) -> generator[string]
```

Strings of :alphanumeric, :alpha, :lower, :digit, :ascii or :printable characters, up to size long, shrinking to shorter and earlier ones.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.string(:digit), 10), fn s -> String.match?(s, ~r/^[0-9]*$/) end)
true
```

### Gen.tuple

```
Gen.tuple(generator[a], generator[b]) -> generator[tuple[a,b]]
Gen.tuple(generator[a], generator[b], generator[c]) -> generator[tuple[a,b,c]]
```

Tuples of two or three generators' values.

```elixir
alx> Enum.all?(Gen.sample(Gen.tuple(Gen.integer(0, 1), Gen.constant("x")), 5), fn {n, s} -> n <= 1 and s == "x" end)
true
```

## Markup

HTML built by ~h templates, which escape every value they interpolate; see alchem syntax templates.

### Markup.escape

```
Markup.escape(string) -> string
```

Text made safe inside an HTML element or a quoted attribute value: &, <, >, " and ' become character references.

```elixir
alx> Markup.escape("<a href='x'>&</a>")
"&lt;a href=&#39;x&#39;&gt;&amp;&lt;/a&gt;"
```

### Markup.join

```
Markup.join(list[Markup]) -> Markup
```

Pieces of markup one after another.

```elixir
alx> items = Enum.map(["a", "b"], fn x -> ~h"<li>#{x}</li>" end)
alx> Markup.to_string(Markup.join(items))
"<li>a</li><li>b</li>"
```

### Markup.of

```
Markup.of(atom) -> Markup
Markup.of(float) -> Markup
Markup.of(Markup) -> Markup
Markup.of(string) -> Markup
Markup.of(integer) -> Markup
Markup.of(list[Markup]) -> Markup
```

What a template does with a value it is given: a string is escaped, markup is kept, a number or atom is written as text and a list of markup is joined.

```elixir
alx> Markup.to_string(Markup.of("1 < 2"))
"1 &lt; 2"
alx> Markup.to_string(Markup.of(~h"<i>kept</i>"))
"<i>kept</i>"
alx> Markup.to_string(Markup.of(42))
"42"
```

### Markup.raw

```
Markup.raw(string) -> Markup
```

Markup made from text exactly as given, for HTML the program trusts: never for text from users.

```elixir
alx> Markup.to_string(Markup.raw("<br>"))
"<br>"
```

### Markup.to_string

```
Markup.to_string(Markup) -> string
```

The HTML text of markup, to send or store.

```elixir
alx> name = "<b>ada</b>"
alx> Markup.to_string(~h"<p>#{name}</p>")
"<p>&lt;b&gt;ada&lt;/b&gt;</p>"
```

## TCP

TCP connections: listen, accept, connect, send and receive text. Calls that wait take milliseconds (negative waits indefinitely) and give error("timeout") or error("closed"); a process waiting in one still stops when asked. A socket belongs to the process that opened it and closes when that process ends.

### TCP.accept

```
TCP.accept(socket, integer) -> result[socket,string]
```

Waits up to the given milliseconds for a connection to a listening socket.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> case TCP.accept(listener, 10) do
...>   ok(_) -> "connected"
...>   error(reason) -> reason
...> end
"timeout"
```

### TCP.address

```
TCP.address(socket) -> string
```

The local address of a socket, host:port.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> String.contains?(TCP.address(listener), ":")
true
```

### TCP.close

```
TCP.close(socket) -> boolean
```

Closes a listener or connection; false when it was already closed. Sockets are also closed when the program ends.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> TCP.close(listener)
true
alx> TCP.close(listener)
false
```

### TCP.connect

```
TCP.connect(string, integer) -> result[socket,string]
TCP.connect(string, integer, list[tuple[atom,atom]]) -> result[socket,string]
```

Connects to an address, waiting up to the given milliseconds.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> server = Task.async(fn ->
...>   ok(client) = TCP.accept(listener, 1000)
...>   ok(line) = TCP.recv_line(client, 1000)
...>   TCP.send(client, String.upcase(line) <> "\n")
...> end)
alx> ok(conn) = TCP.connect(TCP.address(listener), 1000)
alx> TCP.send(conn, "hi\n")
ok({})
alx> TCP.recv_line(conn, 1000)
ok("HI")
```

### TCP.controlling_process

```
TCP.controlling_process(socket, pid[a]) -> boolean
```

Hands a socket to another process, whose end then closes it instead of the opener's.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> keeper: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do
...>   Process.receive(self, 60000)
...>   0
...> end, 1)
alx> TCP.controlling_process(listener, keeper)
true
```

### TCP.listen

```
TCP.listen(string) -> result[socket,string]
TCP.listen(string, list[tuple[atom,atom]]) -> result[socket,string]
```

Listens on an address, host:port; port 0 picks a free one, which TCP.address reports.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> String.starts_with?(TCP.address(listener), "127.0.0.1:")
true
```

### TCP.peer

```
TCP.peer(socket) -> option[string]
```

The address of the other end of a connection; none for a listener.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> TCP.peer(listener)
none
```

### TCP.recv

```
TCP.recv(socket, integer, integer) -> result[string,string]
```

Reads exactly the given number of bytes, or with 0 whatever has arrived once anything has, waiting up to the given milliseconds. error("closed") once the other end has closed.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> server = Task.async(fn ->
...>   ok(client) = TCP.accept(listener, 1000)
...>   ok(line) = TCP.recv_line(client, 1000)
...>   TCP.send(client, String.upcase(line) <> "\n")
...> end)
alx> ok(conn) = TCP.connect(TCP.address(listener), 1000)
alx> TCP.send(conn, "xy\n")
ok({})
alx> TCP.recv(conn, 0, 1000)
ok("XY\n")
alx> TCP.recv(conn, 0, 1000)
error("closed")
```

### TCP.recv_line

```
TCP.recv_line(socket, integer) -> result[string,string]
```

Reads a line, without its newline or a carriage return before it, waiting up to the given milliseconds.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> server = Task.async(fn ->
...>   ok(client) = TCP.accept(listener, 1000)
...>   ok(line) = TCP.recv_line(client, 1000)
...>   TCP.send(client, String.upcase(line) <> "\n")
...> end)
alx> ok(conn) = TCP.connect(TCP.address(listener), 1000)
alx> TCP.send(conn, "line\r\n")
ok({})
alx> TCP.recv_line(conn, 1000)
ok("LINE")
```

### TCP.send

```
TCP.send(socket, string) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Writes text to a connection.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> server = Task.async(fn ->
...>   ok(client) = TCP.accept(listener, 1000)
...>   ok(line) = TCP.recv_line(client, 1000)
...>   TCP.send(client, String.upcase(line) <> "\n")
...> end)
alx> ok(conn) = TCP.connect(TCP.address(listener), 1000)
alx> TCP.send(conn, "abc\n")
ok({})
alx> TCP.recv(conn, 4, 1000)
ok("ABC\n")
```

### TCP.setopts

```
TCP.setopts(socket, list[tuple[atom,atom]]) -> result[tuple[],string]
TCP.setopts(socket, list[tuple[atom,integer]]) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Sets socket options. active: true sends every packet to the controlling process as TCP.Event.data(text), then TCP.Event.closed or TCP.Event.error(reason); active: :once sends one and makes the socket passive again; active: n sends n; active: false stops. The controlling process is the one given to controlling_process, or the opener, and its messages must be TCP.Event. packet: :raw (the default) delivers what has arrived, packet: :line a line with its newline, and packet: 1, 2 or 4 a packet with a length header of that many bytes, which TCP.send adds. TCP.recv with length 0 reads one packet.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> server = Task.async(fn ->
...>   ok(client) = TCP.accept(listener, 1000)
...>   ok(line) = TCP.recv_line(client, 1000)
...>   TCP.send(client, String.upcase(line) <> "\n")
...> end)
alx> ok(conn) = TCP.connect(TCP.address(listener), 1000)
alx> me: pid[TCP.Event] = Process.self(8)
alx> TCP.setopts(conn, [active: :once])
ok({})
alx> TCP.send(conn, "hi\n")
ok({})
alx> Process.receive(me, 1000)
{true, TCP.Event.data("HI\n")}
alx> TCP.setopts(conn, [packet: 4])
ok({})
```

### TCP.shutdown

```
TCP.shutdown(socket, atom) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Closes one direction of a connection: :write tells the other end there is no more to read, :read stops reading, :read_write closes it.

```elixir
alx> ok(listener) = TCP.listen("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> server = Task.async(fn ->
...>   ok(client) = TCP.accept(listener, 1000)
...>   ok(line) = TCP.recv_line(client, 1000)
...>   TCP.send(client, String.upcase(line) <> "\n")
...> end)
alx> ok(conn) = TCP.connect(TCP.address(listener), 1000)
alx> TCP.send(conn, "bye\n")
ok({})
alx> TCP.shutdown(conn, :write)
ok({})
alx> TCP.recv_line(conn, 1000)
ok("BYE")
```

## UDP

UDP sockets: datagrams sent to and received from host:port addresses, passively with UDP.recv or actively as UDP.Event messages. UDP sockets close as TCP sockets do.

### UDP.address

```
UDP.address(socket) -> string
```

The local address of a UDP socket, host:port.

```elixir
alx> ok(socket) = UDP.open("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> String.contains?(UDP.address(socket), ":")
true
```

### UDP.close

```
UDP.close(socket) -> boolean
```

Closes a UDP socket; false when it was already closed.

```elixir
alx> ok(socket) = UDP.open("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> UDP.close(socket)
true
alx> UDP.close(socket)
false
```

### UDP.controlling_process

```
UDP.controlling_process(socket, pid[a]) -> boolean
```

Hands a UDP socket to another process, which then receives its events and whose end closes it.

```elixir
alx> ok(socket) = UDP.open("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> keeper: pid[UDP.Event] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[UDP.Event]): integer do
...>   Process.receive(self, 60000)
...>   0
...> end, 1)
alx> UDP.controlling_process(socket, keeper)
true
```

### UDP.open

```
UDP.open(string) -> result[socket,string]
```

Opens a UDP socket on an address, host:port; port 0 picks a free one, which UDP.address reports.

```elixir
alx> ok(socket) = UDP.open("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> String.starts_with?(UDP.address(socket), "127.0.0.1:")
true
```

### UDP.recv

```
UDP.recv(socket, integer) -> result[tuple[string,string],string]
```

Waits up to the given milliseconds for a datagram: ok({from, text}), or error("timeout").

```elixir
alx> ok(socket) = UDP.open("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> UDP.recv(socket, 10)
error("timeout")
```

### UDP.send

```
UDP.send(socket, string, string) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Sends a datagram to an address.

```elixir
alx> ok(a) = UDP.open("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> ok(b) = UDP.open("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> UDP.send(a, UDP.address(b), "ping")
ok({})
alx> case UDP.recv(b, 1000) do
...>   ok({_, text}) -> text
...>   error(reason) -> reason
...> end
"ping"
```

### UDP.setopts

```
UDP.setopts(socket, list[tuple[atom,atom]]) -> result[tuple[],string]
UDP.setopts(socket, list[tuple[atom,integer]]) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

active: true, :once, false or a number sends datagrams to the controlling process as UDP.Event.datagram(from, text), as TCP.setopts does for TCP.

```elixir
alx> me: pid[UDP.Event] = Process.self(8)
alx> ok(socket) = UDP.open("127.0.0.1:0")
alx> UDP.setopts(socket, [active: :once])
ok({})
alx> UDP.send(socket, UDP.address(socket), "self")
ok({})
alx> case Process.receive(me, 1000) do
...>   {true, UDP.Event.datagram(_, text)} -> text
...>   _ -> "nothing"
...> end
"self"
```

## HTTP

An HTTP client, and a server that answers each request in a process of its own. Requests and responses are the HTTP.Request and HTTP.Response structs; header names are lower case.

### HTTP.address

```
HTTP.address(http_server) -> string
```

The address a server listens on, host:port, with the port chosen when it was 0.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   HTTP.text(200, request.method <> " " <> request.path <> " " <> request.body)
...> end)
alx> String.starts_with?(HTTP.address(server), "127.0.0.1:")
true
```

### HTTP.await

```
HTTP.await(http_server, integer) -> boolean
```

Waits up to the given milliseconds (negative waits indefinitely) for a server to stop; a program that only serves ends main with HTTP.await(server, -1).

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   HTTP.text(200, request.method <> " " <> request.path <> " " <> request.body)
...> end)
alx> HTTP.await(server, 10)
false
```

### HTTP.chunked

```
HTTP.chunked(integer, list[tuple[string,string]], enum[string]) -> HTTP.Response
```

A response whose body is sent as the enumerable gives it, each piece as soon as it is made: a server can stream a large or slow body without holding it whole.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn _ -> HTTP.chunked(200, [], Stream.map(1..3, fn n -> to_string(n) end)) end)
alx> ok(response) = HTTP.get("http://" <> HTTP.address(server))
alx> response.body
"123"
```

### HTTP.get

```
HTTP.get(string) -> result[HTTP.Response,string]
HTTP.get(string, list[tuple[string,string]]) -> result[HTTP.Response,string]
```

Sends a GET request, with optional headers, waiting up to 30 seconds. A response with any status is ok; error is for a request that got no response.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   HTTP.text(200, request.method <> " " <> request.path <> " " <> request.body)
...> end)
alx> base = "http://" <> HTTP.address(server)
alx> ok(response) = HTTP.get(base <> "/a", [{"accept", "text/plain"}])
alx> response.body
"GET /a "
```

### HTTP.header

```
HTTP.header(list[tuple[string,string]], string) -> option[string]
```

The first value of a header, by name in any case.

```elixir
alx> HTTP.header([{"content-type", "text/plain"}], "Content-Type")
some("text/plain")
```

### HTTP.json

```
HTTP.json(integer, JSON) -> HTTP.Response
```

A response with a status and a JSON body.

```elixir
alx> HTTP.json(200, JSON.object(%{"ok" => JSON.boolean(true)})).body
"{\"ok\":true}"
```

### HTTP.match

```
HTTP.match(HTTP.Request, string, string) -> option[map[string,string]]
```

Matches a request against a method (or "*") and a path pattern, whose segments may be :name for one segment or *name for the rest: some of the parameters, or none.

```elixir
alx> request = %HTTP.Request{method: "GET", path: "/users/7", query: "", headers: [], body: ""}
alx> HTTP.match(request, "GET", "/users/:id")
some(%{"id" => "7"})
alx> HTTP.match(request, "GET", "/posts/:id")
none
```

### HTTP.post

```
HTTP.post(string, string, list[tuple[string,string]]) -> result[HTTP.Response,string]
```

Sends a POST request with a body and headers.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   HTTP.text(200, request.method <> " " <> request.path <> " " <> request.body)
...> end)
alx> base = "http://" <> HTTP.address(server)
alx> ok(response) = HTTP.post(base <> "/items", "apple", [{"content-type", "text/plain"}])
alx> response.body
"POST /items apple"
```

### HTTP.read

```
HTTP.read(HTTP.Response) -> string
```

The whole body of a response: its body, followed by its chunks when it has any.

```elixir
alx> HTTP.read(HTTP.chunked(200, [], ["a", "b"]))
"ab"
alx> HTTP.read(HTTP.text(200, "c"))
"c"
```

### HTTP.request

```
HTTP.request(string, string, list[tuple[string,string]], string) -> result[HTTP.Response,string]
HTTP.request(string, string, list[tuple[string,string]], string, integer) -> result[HTTP.Response,string]
HTTP.request(string, string, list[tuple[string,string]], string, list[tuple[atom,string]]) -> result[HTTP.Response,string]
```

Sends a request with any method, headers and body, waiting up to 30 seconds or the given milliseconds; error("timeout") when no response came in time. Options may take the place of the milliseconds: timeout: (as text), ca_file: a PEM file of certificates to trust, insecure: "true" to trust any, and stream: "true" for the body as chunks, as HTTP.stream gives it.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   HTTP.text(200, request.method <> " " <> request.path <> " " <> request.body)
...> end)
alx> base = "http://" <> HTTP.address(server)
alx> ok(response) = HTTP.request("PUT", base <> "/x", [], "v")
alx> response.body
"PUT /x v"
alx> case HTTP.request("GET", "http://127.0.0.1:1/", [], "", 1000) do
...>   ok(_) -> "answered"
...>   error(_) -> "no response"
...> end
"no response"
```

### HTTP.route

```
HTTP.route(HTTP.Request, list[tuple[string,string,fn[HTTP.Request,map[string,string],HTTP.Response]]]) -> HTTP.Response
```

Answers a request with the first of a list of {method, pattern, handler} routes that matches, as HTTP.match does; the handler also gets the parameters. A path no route takes is 404, and one only other methods take is 405 with an allow header.

```elixir
alx> show = fn(_: HTTP.Request, params: map[string, string]): HTTP.Response do HTTP.text(200, Map.get(params, "id", "")) end
alx> request = %HTTP.Request{method: "GET", path: "/users/7", query: "", headers: [], body: ""}
alx> HTTP.route(request, [{"GET", "/users/:id", show}]).body
"7"
alx> HTTP.route(request, [{"POST", "/users/:id", show}]).status
405
```

### HTTP.serve

```
HTTP.serve(string, fn[HTTP.Request,HTTP.Response]) -> result[http_server,string]
HTTP.serve(string, fn[HTTP.Request,HTTP.Response], list[tuple[atom,integer]]) -> result[http_server,string]
```

Serves HTTP on an address, host:port. Each request runs the handler in a process of its own; a handler that fails answers 500. The server stops when HTTP.stop is called or the program ends. A third argument sets limits: read_timeout:, write_timeout:, idle_timeout: (how long a kept-alive connection waits for its next request) and header_timeout: in milliseconds, max_header_bytes:, max_body_bytes: (64 MB by default; larger requests get 413), and keep_alive: 0 to close each connection after one request.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   HTTP.text(200, request.method <> " " <> request.path <> " " <> request.body)
...> end)
alx> base = "http://" <> HTTP.address(server)
alx> ok(response) = HTTP.get(base <> "/hello")
alx> {response.status, response.body}
{200, "GET /hello "}
alx> HTTP.stop(server)
true
```

### HTTP.serve_tls

```
HTTP.serve_tls(string, fn[HTTP.Request,HTTP.Response], list[tuple[atom,string]]) -> result[http_server,string]
HTTP.serve_tls(string, fn[HTTP.Request,HTTP.Response], list[tuple[atom,string]], list[tuple[atom,integer]]) -> result[http_server,string]
```

Serves HTTPS with a certificate and key read from PEM files, given as [certfile: path, keyfile: path], and the same limits as HTTP.serve. Clients trust it through the system's authorities, or HTTP.request with [ca_file: path].

```elixir
alx> case HTTP.serve_tls("127.0.0.1:0", fn _ -> HTTP.text(200, "secure") end, [certfile: "missing.pem", keyfile: "missing.pem"]) do
...>   ok(_) -> "serving"
...>   error(_) -> "no certificate"
...> end
"no certificate"
```

### HTTP.stop

```
HTTP.stop(http_server) -> boolean
```

Stops a server and closes its connections.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   HTTP.text(200, request.method <> " " <> request.path <> " " <> request.body)
...> end)
alx> HTTP.stop(server)
true
alx> HTTP.await(server, 1000)
true
```

### HTTP.stream

```
HTTP.stream(string, string, list[tuple[string,string]], string) -> result[HTTP.Response,string]
```

Sends a request and returns once the head of the response has come, with the body as some(stream) in chunks, read as it arrives: for long or endless responses. HTTP.read reads it whole.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   HTTP.text(200, request.method <> " " <> request.path <> " " <> request.body)
...> end)
alx> base = "http://" <> HTTP.address(server)
alx> ok(response) = HTTP.stream("GET", base <> "/s", [], "")
alx> HTTP.read(response)
"GET /s "
```

### HTTP.text

```
HTTP.text(integer, string) -> HTTP.Response
```

A response with a status and a plain text body.

```elixir
alx> response = HTTP.text(404, "not found")
alx> {response.status, response.body}
{404, "not found"}
```
