## Range

Ranges of integers, first..last//step: a Range struct with first, last and step, and an enumerable of its integers. A range written where a stream is expected is that stream.

### Range.disjoint?

```
Range.disjoint?(Range, Range) -> boolean
```

Reports whether two ranges hold no integer in common.

```elixir
alx> Range.disjoint?(1..5, 6..9)
true
alx> Range.disjoint?(1..5, 5..9)
false
```

### Range.new

```
Range.new(integer, integer) -> Range
Range.new(integer, integer, integer) -> Range
```

The range from first to last, a step of 1 apart, or of a given step.

```elixir
alx> Range.new(1, 3)
1..3
alx> Range.new(0, 10, 5) |> Enum.to_list()
[0, 5, 10]
```

### Range.shift

```
Range.shift(Range, integer) -> Range
```

Moves a range by a number of its steps.

```elixir
alx> Range.shift(1..3, 2)
3..5
```

### Range.size

```
Range.size(Range) -> integer
```

How many integers a range holds.

```elixir
alx> Range.size(1..10)
10
alx> Range.size(1..10//4)
3
alx> Range.size(1..0//1)
0
```

### Range.split

```
Range.split(Range, integer) -> tuple[Range,Range]
```

Splits a range after a number of its integers, or before the last of them for a negative number.

```elixir
alx> Range.split(1..10, 3)
{1..3, 4..10}
```

### Range.to_list

```
Range.to_list(Range) -> list[integer]
```

The integers of a range, in order.

```elixir
alx> Range.to_list(5..1//-2)
[5, 3, 1]
```

## Registry

Finds processes by key. Each entry belongs to the process that registered it, holds a value, and goes away when that process ends.

### Registry.count

```
Registry.count(registry[k,v]) -> integer
```

The number of entries held by living processes.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> worker: pid[integer] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[integer]): integer do
...>   Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 1)
...>   Process.receive(self, 60000)
...>   0
...> end, 1)
alx> Process.sleep(50)
alx> Registry.count(rooms)
1
alx> Process.send(worker, 0, 100)
true
alx> Process.await(worker, 1000)
{true, "normal"}
alx> Registry.count(rooms)
0
```

### Registry.count_match

```
Registry.count_match(registry[k,v], k, fn[v,boolean]) -> integer
```

How many entries under a key have values that pass the test.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 1)
ok({})
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 7)
ok({})
alx> Registry.count_match(rooms, "lobby", fn n -> n > 5 end)
1
```

### Registry.dispatch

```
Registry.dispatch(registry[k,v], k, fn[list[tuple[integer,v]],b]) -> atom
```

Calls the function with the entries under a key, as {process id, value}, when there are any, and returns :ok. Put a pid in the value to send to the processes.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, pid[string]] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(4)
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "news", me)
ok({})
alx> Registry.dispatch(rooms, "news", fn entries -> Enum.each(entries, fn {_, inbox} -> Process.send(inbox, "hello", 100) end) end)
:ok
alx> Process.receive(me, 1000)
{true, "hello"}
```

### Registry.entries

```
Registry.entries(registry[k,v], k) -> list[tuple[integer,v]]
```

The process ids and values registered under a key by living processes, in the order they registered, as Elixir's lookup gives pids and values. Process.id gives a pid's id.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 1)
ok({})
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(4)
alx> Registry.entries(rooms, "lobby") == [{Process.id(me), 1}]
true
```

### Registry.keys

```
Registry.keys(registry[k,v], pid[a]) -> list[k]
```

The keys a process holds.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 1)
ok({})
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(4)
alx> Registry.keys(rooms, me)
["lobby"]
```

### Registry.lookup

```
Registry.lookup(registry[k,v], k) -> list[v]
```

The values registered under a key by living processes, in the order they registered. Elixir also returns each entry's pid; put the pid in the value when it is needed.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 1)
ok({})
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 2)
ok({})
alx> Registry.lookup(rooms, "lobby")
[1, 2]
```

### Registry.match

```
Registry.match(registry[k,v], k, fn[v,boolean]) -> list[tuple[integer,v]]
```

The entries under a key whose values pass the test, as {process id, value}.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 1)
ok({})
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 7)
ok({})
alx> Enum.map(Registry.match(rooms, "lobby", fn n -> n > 5 end), fn {_, n} -> n end)
[7]
```

### Registry.meta

```
Registry.meta(registry[k,v], atom) -> option[m]
```

A value stored with put_meta. Its type comes from the annotation; a value of another type is not found.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> Registry.put_meta(rooms, :owner, "chat")
:ok
alx> owner: option[string] = Registry.meta(rooms, :owner)
alx> owner
some("chat")
```

### Registry.partitions

```
Registry.partitions(registry[k,v]) -> integer
```

The number of partitions; start_link takes [partitions: n] after the keys option. Each partition has its own lock, so processes registering under different keys seldom wait for each other.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate], [partitions: 8])
alx> Registry.partitions(rooms)
8
```

### Registry.put_meta

```
Registry.put_meta(registry[k,v], atom, m) -> atom
```

Stores a value under a name for the whole registry, and returns :ok.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> Registry.put_meta(rooms, :owner, "chat")
:ok
```

### Registry.register

```
Registry.register(registry[k,v], k, v) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Registers the calling process under a key with a value, until it ends or unregisters. In a unique registry a key held by a living process gives error("already_registered").

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> names: registry[atom, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :unique])
alx> Registry.register(names, :alpha, 1)
ok({})
alx> Registry.register(names, :alpha, 2)
error("already_registered")
```

### Registry.select

```
Registry.select(registry[k,v], fn[k,integer,v,boolean]) -> list[tuple[k,integer,v]]
```

Every entry whose key, process id and value pass the test, as {key, process id, value}: what Elixir's select does with a match specification.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 1)
ok({})
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "hall", 2)
ok({})
alx> Enum.map(Registry.select(rooms, fn key, _, _ -> key == "hall" end), fn {key, _, value} -> {key, value} end)
[{"hall", 2}]
```

### Registry.start_link

```
Registry.start_link(list[tuple[atom,atom]]) -> registry[k,v]
Registry.start_link(list[tuple[atom,atom]], list[tuple[atom,integer]]) -> registry[k,v]
```

Starts a registry. keys: :unique allows one living entry per key; keys: :duplicate allows any number, from one process or several. The key and value types come from the annotation; keys are integers, strings, booleans or atoms.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, pid[string]] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> Registry.count(rooms)
0
```

### Registry.unregister

```
Registry.unregister(registry[k,v], k) -> boolean
```

Removes the calling process's entries under a key; false when it had none.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> names: registry[atom, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :unique])
alx> Registry.register(names, :alpha, 1)
ok({})
alx> Registry.unregister(names, :alpha)
true
alx> Registry.lookup(names, :alpha)
[]
```

### Registry.unregister_match

```
Registry.unregister_match(registry[k,v], k, fn[v,boolean]) -> integer
```

Removes the calling process's entries under a key whose values pass the test, and returns how many it removed.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 1)
ok({})
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 7)
ok({})
alx> Registry.unregister_match(rooms, "lobby", fn n -> n > 5 end)
1
alx> Registry.lookup(rooms, "lobby")
[1]
```

### Registry.update_value

```
Registry.update_value(registry[k,v], k, fn[v,v]) -> result[tuple[v,v],string]
```

Replaces the value of the calling process's entry under a key with the function's result: ok({new, old}), or error("not_registered").

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> names: registry[atom, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :unique])
alx> Registry.register(names, :hits, 1)
ok({})
alx> Registry.update_value(names, :hits, fn n -> n + 1 end)
ok({2, 1})
```

### Registry.values

```
Registry.values(registry[k,v], k, pid[a]) -> list[v]
```

The values one process registered under a key.

Requires: k is a map key type.

```elixir
alx> rooms: registry[string, integer] = Registry.start_link([keys: :duplicate])
alx> Registry.register(rooms, "lobby", 1)
ok({})
alx> me: pid[string] = Process.self(4)
alx> Registry.values(rooms, "lobby", me)
[1]
```

## DynamicSupervisor

A supervisor that starts children while it runs, of any message type, and restarts the ones that fail.

### DynamicSupervisor.alive

```
DynamicSupervisor.alive(dynamic_supervisor) -> boolean
```

Reports whether the supervisor is running.

```elixir
alx> sup = DynamicSupervisor.start_link()
alx> DynamicSupervisor.alive(sup)
true
```

### DynamicSupervisor.count_children

```
DynamicSupervisor.count_children(dynamic_supervisor) -> integer
```

How many children are running.

```elixir
alx> sup = DynamicSupervisor.start_link()
alx> DynamicSupervisor.count_children(sup)
0
```

### DynamicSupervisor.restarts

```
DynamicSupervisor.restarts(dynamic_supervisor) -> integer
```

How many times children have been restarted.

```elixir
alx> sup = DynamicSupervisor.start_link()
alx> ok(worker) = DynamicSupervisor.start_child(sup, fn(self: pid[string]): integer do
...>   Process.crash("boom")
...> end)
alx> Process.sleep(50)
alx> DynamicSupervisor.restarts(sup) > 0
true
```

### DynamicSupervisor.start_child

```
DynamicSupervisor.start_child(dynamic_supervisor, fn[pid[a],integer]) -> result[pid[a],string]
DynamicSupervisor.start_child(dynamic_supervisor, fn[pid[a],integer], atom) -> result[pid[a],string]
```

Starts a process under the supervisor and returns its pid. The restart is :permanent (restarted whenever it ends, the default), :transient (restarted when it fails) or :temporary (never restarted). A restarted child is a new process with a new pid.

```elixir
alx> sup = DynamicSupervisor.start_link()
alx> ok(worker) = DynamicSupervisor.start_child(sup, fn(self: pid[string]): integer do
...>   Process.receive(self, 60000)
...>   0
...> end)
alx> DynamicSupervisor.count_children(sup)
1
alx> ok(once) = DynamicSupervisor.start_child(sup, fn(self: pid[string]): integer do 0 end, :temporary)
alx> Process.await(once, 1000)
{true, "normal"}
alx> Process.sleep(20)
alx> DynamicSupervisor.count_children(sup)
1
```

### DynamicSupervisor.start_link

```
DynamicSupervisor.start_link() -> dynamic_supervisor
DynamicSupervisor.start_link(list[tuple[atom,integer]]) -> dynamic_supervisor
```

Starts a supervisor with no children. It gives up, stopping its children, after more than max_restarts restarts within max_seconds: 3 within 5 unless the options say otherwise. With max_children: it runs at most that many children at once, and start_child returns error("max_children") beyond them.

```elixir
alx> sup = DynamicSupervisor.start_link()
alx> DynamicSupervisor.count_children(sup)
0
alx> strict = DynamicSupervisor.start_link([max_restarts: 1, max_seconds: 10])
alx> DynamicSupervisor.alive(strict)
true
```

### DynamicSupervisor.start_server

```
DynamicSupervisor.start_server(dynamic_supervisor, s, fn[s,q,tuple[s,r]]) -> result[server[q,r],string]
```

Starts a server under the supervisor. The server restarts itself after a handler failure, within the supervisor's limits, so its handle stays good; it stops when the supervisor stops.

```elixir
alx> sup = DynamicSupervisor.start_link()
alx> ok(counter) = DynamicSupervisor.start_server(sup, 0, fn(total: integer, amount: integer): tuple[integer, integer] do {total + amount, total + amount} end)
alx> Server.call(counter, 2, 1000)
ok(2)
alx> DynamicSupervisor.stop(sup)
true
alx> Server.alive(counter)
false
```

### DynamicSupervisor.stop

```
DynamicSupervisor.stop(dynamic_supervisor) -> boolean
```

Stops the supervisor and its children, waiting up to five seconds; true when they ended.

```elixir
alx> sup = DynamicSupervisor.start_link()
alx> DynamicSupervisor.stop(sup)
true
alx> DynamicSupervisor.alive(sup)
false
```

### DynamicSupervisor.terminate_child

```
DynamicSupervisor.terminate_child(dynamic_supervisor, pid[a]) -> boolean
```

Stops a child and forgets it, so it is not restarted; false when the pid is not a child.

```elixir
alx> sup = DynamicSupervisor.start_link()
alx> ok(worker) = DynamicSupervisor.start_child(sup, fn(self: pid[string]): integer do
...>   Process.receive(self, 60000)
...>   0
...> end)
alx> DynamicSupervisor.terminate_child(sup, worker)
true
alx> DynamicSupervisor.count_children(sup)
0
alx> DynamicSupervisor.terminate_child(sup, worker)
false
```

### DynamicSupervisor.which_children

```
DynamicSupervisor.which_children(dynamic_supervisor) -> list[integer]
```

The process ids of the running children, in the order they were started.

```elixir
alx> sup = DynamicSupervisor.start_link()
alx> ok(worker) = DynamicSupervisor.start_child(sup, fn(self: pid[string]): integer do
...>   Process.receive(self, 60000)
...>   0
...> end)
alx> DynamicSupervisor.which_children(sup) == [Process.id(worker)]
true
```

## WebSocket

WebSockets, RFC 6455: a handler of HTTP.serve upgrades its request into a socket, and WebSocket.connect opens one to a server. Messages are text or binary; pings and the closing handshake are answered without the program's help. Calls that wait take milliseconds and give error("timeout") or error("closed"). A socket belongs to the process that made it and closes when that process ends, so a handler that upgrades either keeps the socket or hands it on with controlling_process.

### WebSocket.close

```
WebSocket.close(websocket) -> boolean
WebSocket.close(websocket, integer, string) -> boolean
```

Closes with code 1000, or with a code from 3000 to 4999 and a reason of at most 123 bytes, waiting up to a second for the other end to answer. false when the socket was already closed.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   case WebSocket.upgrade(request) do
...>     ok(ws) ->
...>       answered: result[tuple[], string] = case WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000) do
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.text(text)) -> WebSocket.send(ws, String.upcase(text))
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.binary(data)) -> WebSocket.send_binary(ws, data)
...>         _ -> ok({})
...>       end
...>       if answered == ok({}) do
...>         WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000)
...>       end
...>       HTTP.text(200, "")
...>     error(reason) -> HTTP.text(400, reason)
...>   end
...> end)
alx> ok(ws) = WebSocket.connect("ws://" <> HTTP.address(server) <> "/echo", 1000)
alx> WebSocket.close(ws)
true
alx> WebSocket.close(ws)
false
alx> WebSocket.send(ws, "late")
error("closed")
```

### WebSocket.connect

```
WebSocket.connect(string, integer) -> result[websocket,string]
WebSocket.connect(string, integer, list[tuple[atom,string]]) -> result[websocket,string]
WebSocket.connect(string, integer, list[tuple[atom,string]], list[tuple[string,string]]) -> result[websocket,string]
```

Opens a WebSocket to a ws:// or wss:// address, waiting up to the given milliseconds for the connection and the handshake. Options, as text: ca_file: a PEM file of certificates to trust, insecure: "true" to trust any, and origin: the Origin header to send. A list of {name, value} headers after the options is sent with the handshake, such as a Cookie or Authorization; the headers the handshake sets itself are refused.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   case WebSocket.upgrade(request) do
...>     ok(ws) ->
...>       answered: result[tuple[], string] = case WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000) do
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.text(text)) -> WebSocket.send(ws, String.upcase(text))
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.binary(data)) -> WebSocket.send_binary(ws, data)
...>         _ -> ok({})
...>       end
...>       if answered == ok({}) do
...>         WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000)
...>       end
...>       HTTP.text(200, "")
...>     error(reason) -> HTTP.text(400, reason)
...>   end
...> end)
alx> ok(ws) = WebSocket.connect("ws://" <> HTTP.address(server) <> "/echo", 1000)
alx> WebSocket.send(ws, "hi")
ok({})
alx> WebSocket.recv(ws, 1000)
ok(WebSocket.Event.text("HI"))
alx> case WebSocket.connect("http://" <> HTTP.address(server), 1000) do
...>   ok(_) -> "connected"
...>   error(reason) -> reason
...> end
"a WebSocket address starts with ws:// or wss://"
```

### WebSocket.controlling_process

```
WebSocket.controlling_process(websocket, pid[a]) -> boolean
```

Hands a socket to another process, whose end then closes it and to which an active socket sends its events.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   case WebSocket.upgrade(request) do
...>     ok(ws) ->
...>       answered: result[tuple[], string] = case WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000) do
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.text(text)) -> WebSocket.send(ws, String.upcase(text))
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.binary(data)) -> WebSocket.send_binary(ws, data)
...>         _ -> ok({})
...>       end
...>       if answered == ok({}) do
...>         WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000)
...>       end
...>       HTTP.text(200, "")
...>     error(reason) -> HTTP.text(400, reason)
...>   end
...> end)
alx> ok(ws) = WebSocket.connect("ws://" <> HTTP.address(server) <> "/echo", 1000)
alx> keeper: pid[WebSocket.Event] = Process.spawn(fn(self: pid[WebSocket.Event]): integer do
...>   Process.receive(self, 60000)
...>   0
...> end, 1)
alx> WebSocket.controlling_process(ws, keeper)
true
```

### WebSocket.peer

```
WebSocket.peer(websocket) -> string
```

The address of the other end, host:port.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   case WebSocket.upgrade(request) do
...>     ok(ws) ->
...>       answered: result[tuple[], string] = case WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000) do
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.text(text)) -> WebSocket.send(ws, String.upcase(text))
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.binary(data)) -> WebSocket.send_binary(ws, data)
...>         _ -> ok({})
...>       end
...>       if answered == ok({}) do
...>         WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000)
...>       end
...>       HTTP.text(200, "")
...>     error(reason) -> HTTP.text(400, reason)
...>   end
...> end)
alx> ok(ws) = WebSocket.connect("ws://" <> HTTP.address(server) <> "/echo", 1000)
alx> String.starts_with?(WebSocket.peer(ws), "127.0.0.1:")
true
```

### WebSocket.recv

```
WebSocket.recv(websocket, integer) -> result[WebSocket.Event,string]
```

Waits up to the given milliseconds for the next event: a text or binary message, WebSocket.Event.closed(code, reason) when the other end closes, or WebSocket.Event.error(reason) when the connection fails. After the last event it is error("closed").

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   case WebSocket.upgrade(request) do
...>     ok(ws) ->
...>       answered: result[tuple[], string] = case WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000) do
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.text(text)) -> WebSocket.send(ws, String.upcase(text))
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.binary(data)) -> WebSocket.send_binary(ws, data)
...>         _ -> ok({})
...>       end
...>       if answered == ok({}) do
...>         WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000)
...>       end
...>       HTTP.text(200, "")
...>     error(reason) -> HTTP.text(400, reason)
...>   end
...> end)
alx> ok(ws) = WebSocket.connect("ws://" <> HTTP.address(server) <> "/echo", 1000)
alx> WebSocket.recv(ws, 10)
error("timeout")
alx> WebSocket.send(ws, "x")
ok({})
alx> WebSocket.recv(ws, 1000)
ok(WebSocket.Event.text("X"))
alx> WebSocket.close(ws)
true
alx> WebSocket.recv(ws, 1000)
ok(WebSocket.Event.closed(1000, ""))
alx> WebSocket.recv(ws, 1000)
error("closed")
```

### WebSocket.send

```
WebSocket.send(websocket, string) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Sends a text message.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   case WebSocket.upgrade(request) do
...>     ok(ws) ->
...>       answered: result[tuple[], string] = case WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000) do
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.text(text)) -> WebSocket.send(ws, String.upcase(text))
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.binary(data)) -> WebSocket.send_binary(ws, data)
...>         _ -> ok({})
...>       end
...>       if answered == ok({}) do
...>         WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000)
...>       end
...>       HTTP.text(200, "")
...>     error(reason) -> HTTP.text(400, reason)
...>   end
...> end)
alx> ok(ws) = WebSocket.connect("ws://" <> HTTP.address(server) <> "/echo", 1000)
alx> WebSocket.send(ws, "abc")
ok({})
alx> WebSocket.recv(ws, 1000)
ok(WebSocket.Event.text("ABC"))
```

### WebSocket.send_binary

```
WebSocket.send_binary(websocket, string) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

Sends a binary message: any bytes, which arrive as WebSocket.Event.binary.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   case WebSocket.upgrade(request) do
...>     ok(ws) ->
...>       answered: result[tuple[], string] = case WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000) do
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.text(text)) -> WebSocket.send(ws, String.upcase(text))
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.binary(data)) -> WebSocket.send_binary(ws, data)
...>         _ -> ok({})
...>       end
...>       if answered == ok({}) do
...>         WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000)
...>       end
...>       HTTP.text(200, "")
...>     error(reason) -> HTTP.text(400, reason)
...>   end
...> end)
alx> ok(ws) = WebSocket.connect("ws://" <> HTTP.address(server) <> "/echo", 1000)
alx> WebSocket.send_binary(ws, "\x01\xff")
ok({})
alx> WebSocket.recv(ws, 1000)
ok(WebSocket.Event.binary("\x01\xff"))
```

### WebSocket.setopts

```
WebSocket.setopts(websocket, list[tuple[atom,atom]]) -> result[tuple[],string]
```

active: true sends every event to the controlling process as a WebSocket.Event message, active: :once sends one, and active: false stops. The controlling process is the one given to controlling_process, or the socket's maker, and its messages must be WebSocket.Event.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   case WebSocket.upgrade(request) do
...>     ok(ws) ->
...>       answered: result[tuple[], string] = case WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000) do
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.text(text)) -> WebSocket.send(ws, String.upcase(text))
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.binary(data)) -> WebSocket.send_binary(ws, data)
...>         _ -> ok({})
...>       end
...>       if answered == ok({}) do
...>         WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000)
...>       end
...>       HTTP.text(200, "")
...>     error(reason) -> HTTP.text(400, reason)
...>   end
...> end)
alx> ok(ws) = WebSocket.connect("ws://" <> HTTP.address(server) <> "/echo", 1000)
alx> me: pid[WebSocket.Event] = Process.self(8)
alx> WebSocket.setopts(ws, [active: :once])
ok({})
alx> WebSocket.send(ws, "hi")
ok({})
alx> Process.receive(me, 1000)
{true, WebSocket.Event.text("HI")}
```

### WebSocket.upgrade

```
WebSocket.upgrade(HTTP.Request) -> result[websocket,string]
WebSocket.upgrade(HTTP.Request, list[tuple[atom,integer]]) -> result[websocket,string]
```

Called by an HTTP.serve handler, answers its request with the WebSocket handshake and returns the socket. The response the handler returns afterwards is not sent. A request that is not a WebSocket handshake is error("not a WebSocket request: ..."), and the handler answers it as it likes. [max_message_bytes: n] bounds incoming messages (16 MB by default); a larger one closes the socket with code 1009. Check HTTP.header(request, "origin") before upgrading when only your own pages should connect.

```elixir
alx> ok(server) = HTTP.serve("127.0.0.1:0", fn request ->
...>   case WebSocket.upgrade(request) do
...>     ok(ws) ->
...>       answered: result[tuple[], string] = case WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000) do
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.text(text)) -> WebSocket.send(ws, String.upcase(text))
...>         ok(WebSocket.Event.binary(data)) -> WebSocket.send_binary(ws, data)
...>         _ -> ok({})
...>       end
...>       if answered == ok({}) do
...>         WebSocket.recv(ws, 5000)
...>       end
...>       HTTP.text(200, "")
...>     error(reason) -> HTTP.text(400, reason)
...>   end
...> end)
alx> ok(ws) = WebSocket.connect("ws://" <> HTTP.address(server) <> "/echo", 1000)
alx> WebSocket.send(ws, "hello")
ok({})
alx> WebSocket.recv(ws, 1000)
ok(WebSocket.Event.text("HELLO"))
alx> ok(plain) = HTTP.get("http://" <> HTTP.address(server) <> "/echo")
alx> {plain.status, plain.body}
{400, "not a WebSocket request: no upgrade to websocket"}
```

## Crypto

Cryptographic building blocks: random bytes from the operating system's secure source, hashes, HMAC signatures and a comparison that takes the same time however much of its input matches. Results are raw bytes; Base.encode16 or Base.encode64 makes them printable.

### Crypto.hash

```
Crypto.hash(atom, string) -> string
```

The digest of some data with :md5, :sha1, :sha224, :sha256, :sha384 or :sha512, as raw bytes. MD5 and SHA-1 are for checking old formats, not for security.

```elixir
alx> Base.encode16(Crypto.hash(:sha256, "abc"), [case: :lower])
"ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad"
```

### Crypto.hmac

```
Crypto.hmac(atom, string, string) -> string
```

The HMAC of data under a key with one of the hash algorithms, as raw bytes: a signature only someone holding the key can make. Compare signatures with Crypto.secure_compare.

```elixir
alx> Base.encode16(Crypto.hmac(:sha256, "Jefe", "what do ya want for nothing?"), [case: :lower])
"5bdcc146bf60754e6a042426089575c75a003f089d2739839dec58b964ec3843"
```

### Crypto.secure_compare

```
Crypto.secure_compare(string, string) -> boolean
```

Reports whether two strings are equal, taking a time that depends only on their lengths, so that checking a signature or token does not reveal how much of a guess was right.

```elixir
alx> Crypto.secure_compare("token", "token")
true
alx> Crypto.secure_compare("token", "tokem")
false
```

### Crypto.strong_rand_bytes

```
Crypto.strong_rand_bytes(integer) -> string
```

The given number of random bytes from the operating system's secure source, for keys, tokens and nonces.

```elixir
alx> byte_size(Crypto.strong_rand_bytes(16))
16
alx> Crypto.strong_rand_bytes(16) == Crypto.strong_rand_bytes(16)
false
```
